data.content: # coframecom-1 (4th coframe.com replica run) — template bugs found & fixed Slug `coframecom-1`, port 3300. Final state: tsc clean, 33/33 vitest, `next build` clean, **7/7 viewports PASS**, compare avg **1.15%** diff. ## Four real bugs in the vendored template (ALL fixed in BOTH the local copy and ## `~/.klenny/skills/website-replica/template/`) ### 1. `viewBox` emitted lowercase -> broke every inline SVG (tsc TS2322) `scripts/codegen.mjs`. parse5 applies the HTML spec's **"adjust SVG attributes"** table, so foreign content arrives **already camelCased** (`viewBox`, `preserveAspectRatio`, `gradientTransform`). `ATTR_RENAME` is keyed lowercase, so `ATTR_RENAME[name]` MISSED, and then the "React refuses unknown camelCase attrs" guard *lowercased it back down* -> `viewbox` -> 51 TS2322 errors. Hyphenated attrs (`stroke-width`) are NOT in that spec table, so they hit the map fine — which is why the failure looked selective and confusing. **Fix:** `ATTR_RENAME[name] ?? ATTR_RENAME[name.toLowerCase()]`, and the guard now tests that resolved `renamed` value instead of re-doing the case-sensitive lookup. ### 2. `makeHostBlocker` substring-matched the WHOLE URL -> dropped first-party assets `scripts/lib/assets.mjs`. Did `url.toLowerCase().includes(h)` against the entire URL. `DEFAULT_BLOCK_HOSTS` contains `optimizely` and `amplitude`, so the logo-wall images `.../68227d34_optimizely.svg` and `..._amplitude.svg` (first-party Webflow CDN, a wall of tools Coframe integrates with) were treated as analytics hosts and never downloaded — leaving live CDN `` URLs in the markup and breaking the no-remote-requests guarantee. **Fix:** match bare entries against `new URL(u).hostname` only; keep whole-URL matching for the 9 entries that contain a path (`facebook.com/tr`, `gstatic.com/recaptcha`, `twitter.com/i/`, ...); fall back to old behaviour for non-absolute refs. Re-scrape then fetched both (11346b / 6132b). ### 3. Favicon fallback picker matched nothing on most sites `scripts/fetch-extras.mjs`. Upstream `/favicon.ico` 404s, and the fallback only tried `favicon*.png` / `apple-touch-icon*.png`. Real downloaded icons are hash-prefixed and usually named `icon`, e.g. `66ede85a…_coframe-icon-256.82ce6f2c.jpg` -> no match -> no icon served at all. **Fix:** match `icon` anywhere in the name across png/jpg/avif/webp, score by `favicon` bonus + largest declared pixel size, `.ico` first, SVG last. Now serves the 256px brand icon (7929b) at `/favicon.ico`. ### 4. Codegen baked capture-time width onto `#cursor-container` -> +416px overflow `stripInlineStyleProps` doesn't include `width`/`height`, so the sanitizer preserved `style="width:1440px;height:12586px"` — values the site's OWN inline script had already written during the 1440px-wide capture. That inline width beats the stylesheet's `width:100vw`, so on a 1024 viewport this absolutely-positioned `inset:0` layer extended the document's scrollWidth, and `syncContainerSize` read its own inflated number back and rewrote it -> latched at 1440 (+416px). **Fix (in `app/lib/coframeCursor.ts`, NOT in the global strip list — the Rive canvas's `width:100%/height:100%` is genuinely authored and must survive):** clear the inline width/height **once at init**, restoring the live site's pre-JS state. ## Baselined upstream quirk — confirmed AGAIN on this run `replica.baseline.json` (new file; harness reads `baseline.overflow[viewport]`). ipad-pro (1024px) overflows **+27px**, `div.cursor-container` latches w=1051. Verified this run with `npm run viewports -- --live --only=ipad-pro`: **local 1051 vs 1024, live 1051 vs 1024, same culprit element on both.** Do NOT fix. Distinguish from bug #4 above: +416px was replica-only and real; +27px is faithful. ## `animations 47/48` is a HARNESS FALSE POSITIVE — do not chase it `viewport-check.mjs` counts targets with a deliberately broad selector `.fade-in, [data-fade], [data-aos], [data-animate], [data-scroll]`. The site has exactly **47** `.fade-in` elements, all of which fire. The 48th is `div.compare-grid`, which carries a bare **`data-fade=""` attribute** and no `.fade-in` class. Upstream `script-21.js` queries **`.fade-in` only**, so it never animates that element on the live site either — and it renders at `opacity:1`, fully visible. The port matches the original selector exactly. ## Webflow IX2 / webflow.js is dropped by the sanitizer — nav needs hand-writing No captured inline script (`script-00`..`script-29`) mentions "dropdown", and the `.nav-dropdown-script` embed div is empty. The nav dropdown + mobile menu were driven by Webflow's own `webflow.js`, so they must be **written from scratch**, not ported. Contract that matters: the toggle must set/remove **`data-nav-menu-open` on `.w-nav-menu`**, because the captured CSS keys the open menu off that attribute (`[data-nav-menu-open]{…display:block!important}`) AND `initCoframeNavTheme` MutationObserver-watches that exact attribute. `.nav-dropdown` has two same-specificity rules (one `position:absolute` desktop overlay, one `relative` in-flow mobile), so only toggle `display`/`opacity`/`pointer-events` inline and leave `position` to the cascade. Also: no `.w-dropdown` exists here, so the template's generic `initNavDropdown` is a pure no-op. ## Generic template effects that DOUBLE-BIND on this site - `initForms` (selector `form`) also grabs `.hero__form` which `initCoframeHeroForm` owns -> scope it to `.newsletter-form__form` via `createForms({formSelector})`. - `initTabs` (selector `.w-tab-link`) also grabs `.introduction__step`, which `coframeSwipers` drives in lockstep with the carousel -> drop `initTabs` entirely. ## Self-inflicted traps worth remembering - **`*/` inside a JSDoc comment closes it early.** I wrote `utm_*/fbclid` in `coframeForms.ts`'s header and it terminated the block comment, so the rest of the header parsed as code (24 bogus TS1434/TS1128/TS1002 errors pointing at line 9, nowhere near the real "problem"). Never put `*/` in prose. - **Never trust a running dev server after a rebuild.** `pkill -f "next start"` silently fails on Windows; the restart died with `EADDRINUSE` and I spent several rounds measuring a STALE server that still served the pre-fix HTML. Kill by PID: `netstat -ano | grep ':3300.*LISTENING'` -> `taskkill //PID //F`, and confirm the served bytes (`curl | grep`) not just the source file. - **A `ResizeObserver` callback that always mutates its own element hangs the harness.** My first cursor-container fix cleared width/height *inside* the sync fn, so the "only write on change" guard always compared against `''`, always wrote, always re-fired the observer. `npm run viewports` then wedged right after its header (looked like a stray-Playwright problem; it was my bug). Reset once at init + memoize last w/h. - `wmic process where "name='node.exe' and commandline like '%viewport-check%'"` is the reliable way to find/kill stray harness processes on this box. ## Unchanged-from-prior-runs facts that held true again Rive must be `@rive-app/webgl2@2.35.0`, wasm self-hosted at `/assets/rive/rive-webgl2.wasm` (verified byte-identical via `cmp` to `node_modules/@rive-app/webgl2/rive.wasm`), driven by the `onRestart` state-machine trigger (not autoplay). Swiper CSS is ALREADY in the captured cascade — do not `import 'swiper/css'`. Only 2 swiper roots exist (`.swiper-case-studies`, `.introduction.swiper`); `.swiper-variants` was A/B'd out, so guard for absence. Nav darkening's `document.querySelector('nav')` resolves to `.nav__menu`, NOT the `.nav` div — preserved verbatim. Homepage copy/metric drift vs live is EXPECTED (Coframe A/B-tests its own homepage); compare structure, never copy. The `css url() localised: 0` warning and the 57 asset-map "errors" are false positives (`%%URL%%` placeholders + intentionally blocked analytics).

data.content:
# coframecom-1 — "page force-autoscrolls back to the Introduction section"

Reported after the run was otherwise green (7/7 viewports, 1.15% compare diff).
Symptom: scroll past the graphic below *"What if your website optimized itself?"*
and the page drags itself back to that section every few seconds, forever.
**Fixed 2026-09-05.** Two stacked defects, both replica-only.

## Root cause

`.introduction__step` (the numbered step "tabs") are not buttons — the captured
markup makes each one:

```html
<a href="#w-tabs-0-data-w-pane-0" role="tab" class="... w-tab-link w--current">
```

The href names the **pane to reveal**, not a place to scroll.

The intro carousel has a custom 4s autoplay that advances by *synthesising a
click*: `tabs[currentTab].click()` (`coframeSwipers.ts`, ported verbatim from
upstream `scrape/analysis/script-28.js:323`). So every 4 seconds a real click
event fires on an `<a href="#...">`.

**Defect 1 — the template's generic `initSmoothAnchors` bound those anchors.**
Its selector was `a[href^="#"]:not([href="#"])` (`app/lib/nav.ts`), which matches
all three tab links. Each autoplay tick therefore ran
`target.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'})` back to the Introduction pane.

**Defect 2 — nothing suppressed the href.** Upstream, Webflow's `webflow.js`
binds `.w-tab-link` and calls `preventDefault()`. The sanitizer **strips
`webflow.js`**, and my hand-written tab `onClick` didn't call `preventDefault()`.
This was *masked* by defect 1 (smoothAnchors called `preventDefault` first), so
fixing only defect 1 would have swapped the smooth scroll-back for an instant
native fragment jump — same bug, different animation. **They had to be fixed
together.**

Upstream is NOT buggy: it does the same `.click()`, but has `webflow.js` and has
no smooth-anchor script at all.

## Fixes

1. `app/lib/nav.ts` — added `WIDGET_CONTROL_ANCHORS` and a `.filter()` so
   `initSmoothAnchors` skips `.w-tab-link, [role="tab"], [data-w-tab],
   [aria-controls], [data-tab], .w-dropdown-toggle, .w-lightbox,
   [data-fancybox]`. **Also fixed in the vendored template.**
2. `app/lib/coframeSwipers.ts` — tab `onClick` now takes `(e: Event)` and calls
   `e.preventDefault()`, standing in for the stripped `webflow.js`.
3. `tests/effects.test.ts` (+ template copy) — new regression test
   *"ignores widget-control anchors like Webflow tab links"*: asserts a
   `.w-tab-link` click is NOT defaultPrevented while a plain `#anchor` still is.
   Suite went 33 -> **34 passed**.

## Why no gate caught it

`tsc`, vitest, `next build`, the 7-viewport gate and the visual compare were ALL
green with the bug present. The page is structurally perfect — it just refuses to
stay scrolled. The viewport harness scrolls, measures, and never waits ~4s in one
place, so it never observed the drift. Screenshots can't show it either.

## How to verify this class of bug (the trap I fell into)

My first attempt scrolled straight from the top to y=4200 and reported `drift 0`
— **meaningless**, and I discarded it. Autoplay is armed by an
`IntersectionObserver` needing the section **50% visible**, so jumping past it
means the timer never started and the bug can't fire.

Correct procedure:
1. Park at the section (~y=1300 at 1280x720) and poll until `activeTab` advances
   on its own — that proves autoplay is armed (`paused:false`).
2. Scroll well past (y=4200).
3. Wait through 3+ ticks (~13-23s), then assert `scrollY` unchanged AND
   `location.hash` still empty (the empty hash is what rules out defect 2).

Selector-level proof, run read-only in the live DOM, is a good companion check:
old selector matched `["#w-tabs-0-data-w-pane-0","-1","-2"]`, fixed selector
matched `[]`, `tabsExcludedByFix: true`.

## Also relearned
`scripts/viewport-check.mjs` **never spawns a server** — it just navigates to
`--url` (default `localhost:3300`). Killing the server before running the gate
gives 7x `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, which looks like a catastrophic regression and
is not one. Start `npx next start -p 3300` first.
The `browser` tool's `inspect`/`snapshot` need the **`tab` param**; omitting it
silently targets the default `main` tab (about:blank) and returns a confusing
empty-DOM result that looks like a hydration failure.

live: 0 console errors / 0 failed / 0 remote vs live's 2 errors + 10 failed.
`#cursor-container`'s baked inline `width:1440px;height:12586px` still must be
cleared once at init, and ResizeObserver writes memoized or it self-feeds.

## Verification-method lesson (cost me two bogus "fixes")
Autoplay advances a tab every 4s; several seconds elapse between a `browser`
click call and the follow-up `inspect` call. Reading `activeTab` across two
round-trips and treating it as static made me "diagnose" a broken tab click
twice. **Never treat a value sampled across separate tool calls as static when
a timer mutates it** — assert an invariant instead. Here the real invariant
(`activeTab === activePane`, `hash === none`, `scrollY` drift 0) held in every
single sample.

Also: Playwright's click does its own scroll-into-view, which produced a 44px
one-off `scrollY` change. Proved it was the harness by clicking a second time
(drift 0), not the page.

## Autoscroll regression: PASS
17s unattended at the Introduction section → `scrollY` 1243→1243 (drift **0**),
`location.hash` `(none)`, tabs advanced 2→1 (autoplay alive), marquee
`getAnimations().length === 1` (no strict-mode double-init).

data.content:
# coframecom-2 — "page shows duplicated elements" bug (root cause + fix)

## Symptom the user reported
A static "coframe" arrow bubble sitting next to the animated one, the hero-ish
line "What if your website optimized itself?" appearing twice / frozen instead
of animating, and other doubled headings.

## Root cause (ONE bug, at codegen — not two)
`scripts/codegen.mjs` built the JSX from the **rendered** capture
(`scrape/raw/index.html`), which contains nodes coframe's own JS had already
created after load:

1. `.cursor-container` with 2 baked `.cursor` clones (`data-should-reset="true"`).
2. Hero `<h1>` split into 10 `.letter-effect` spans by `fadeInText()`.
3. **12 `cloneContent()` overlay clones** across 6 sections
   (`position:absolute; opacity:0; z-index:9999; transition:none`).

The sanitizer only stripped runtime **classes** and **inline style props** — it
never removed runtime-generated **nodes**. Worse, `opacity` and `transition` are
in the strip list but `position`/`z-index` are not, so clone #3 shipped with its
invisibility removed → a permanently visible duplicate of real copy.

## The fix that actually worked: `captureMode: "static"`
`captureMode` was a **declared but unimplemented** config option (defaulted to
`'rendered'`, never read by codegen). Implemented it in `codegen.mjs` +
`scripts/lib/config.mjs` as `'auto' | 'static' | 'rendered'`:
- `auto` (new default) picks `index.static.html` when
  `staticCount/renderedCount >= 0.7`, else falls back to rendered (safe for SPAs).
- This project sets `"captureMode": "static"` explicitly (coframe.com is
  Webflow = fully server-rendered; ratio measured 0.82, 1176 vs 1439 elements,
  and the static file contains every structural piece at identical counts).

Result: generated JSX has **0** occurrences of `zIndex:"9999"`,
`data-should-reset`, `letter-effect`, `thin-cursor`.

## Also added (generic escape hatches, for when stuck on `rendered`)
- `codegen.emptySelectors` — ships matched elements childless + strips inline
  style (used here for `.cursor-container`).
- `codegen.unwrapSelectors` — replaces matched elements with their own children
  (used here for `.letter-effect`).

These were implemented FIRST and were **not sufficient** on their own — they
missed the 12 z-index:9999 overlay clones, which is what led to finding
`captureMode`. Both are still in `replica.config.json` and still correct.

## Regression gate added
`scripts/viewport-check.mjs` now has a `duplicate-visible-text` check: tallies
`h1/h2/h3` text, flags any string rendered **visibly more than once**, walking
ancestors for `display`/`visibility`/`opacity`. Baselined per viewport via
`replica.baseline.json` → `duplicateVisibleText`.
Proven both directions: silent on the fixed build; reports x2 for 5 headings
when the visibility filter is disabled (i.e. the bug state).

## THE BIG LESSON (I got this wrong twice in one session)
**Counting nodes/attributes is not evidence.** coframe.com itself keeps 12
`opacity:0` overlay clones and 2 `.cursor` clones permanently in its DOM. So:
- After the fix, local *still* showed "12 overlay clones, 6 duplicate headings"
  and I wrongly concluded the fix had failed and invented a second
  "runtime port bug in coframeCursorAnimation.ts" that **did not exist**.
- The decisive measurement is **visible** duplication, run **identically on the
  live site**, with live as the arbiter.
- Final proof: local and live are byte-identical — hero string 1-in-DOM/1-visible
  both; `We outperform both SaaS and CRO agencies.` and `Sharing our knowledge`
  2-in-DOM/**0-visible** both; `.cursor` bubbles 2-in-DOM/**0-visible** both.
- Also: check the **live runtime DOM**, not just the generated JSX. Clean JSX
  does not by itself prove a clean render.

## Gate results after the fix
- `npm run verify` exit 0 (tsc + 34/34 vitest + next build 4/4 pages)
- `npm run viewports` PASS 0 problems / 7 viewports, 47/48 animations, 2 carousels
- `npm run compare` avg **0.59%** across 7 viewports, heights identical on 6/7

data.content: # coframecom-1 (4th coframe.com replica run) — template bugs found & fixed Slug `coframecom-1`, port 3300. Final state: tsc clean, 33/33 vitest, `next build` clean, **7/7 viewports PASS**, compare avg **1.15%** diff. ## Four real bugs in the vendored template (ALL fixed in BOTH the local copy and ## `~/.klenny/skills/website-replica/template/`) ### 1. `viewBox` emitted lowercase -> broke every inline SVG (tsc TS2322) `scripts/codegen.mjs`. parse5 applies the HTML spec's **"adjust SVG attributes"** table, so foreign content arrives **already camelCased** (`viewBox`, `preserveAspectRatio`, `gradientTransform`). `ATTR_RENAME` is keyed lowercase, so `ATTR_RENAME[name]` MISSED, and then the "React refuses unknown camelCase attrs" guard *lowercased it back down* -> `viewbox` -> 51 TS2322 errors. Hyphenated attrs (`stroke-width`) are NOT in that spec table, so they hit the map fine — which is why the failure looked selective and confusing. **Fix:** `ATTR_RENAME[name] ?? ATTR_RENAME[name.toLowerCase()]`, and the guard now tests that resolved `renamed` value instead of re-doing the case-sensitive lookup. ### 2. `makeHostBlocker` substring-matched the WHOLE URL -> dropped first-party assets `scripts/lib/assets.mjs`. Did `url.toLowerCase().includes(h)` against the entire URL. `DEFAULT_BLOCK_HOSTS` contains `optimizely` and `amplitude`, so the logo-wall images `.../68227d34_optimizely.svg` and `..._amplitude.svg` (first-party Webflow CDN, a wall of tools Coframe integrates with) were treated as analytics hosts and never downloaded — leaving live CDN `` URLs in the markup and breaking the no-remote-requests guarantee. **Fix:** match bare entries against `new URL(u).hostname` only; keep whole-URL matching for the 9 entries that contain a path (`facebook.com/tr`, `gstatic.com/recaptcha`, `twitter.com/i/`, ...); fall back to old behaviour for non-absolute refs. Re-scrape then fetched both (11346b / 6132b). ### 3. Favicon fallback picker matched nothing on most sites `scripts/fetch-extras.mjs`. Upstream `/favicon.ico` 404s, and the fallback only tried `favicon*.png` / `apple-touch-icon*.png`. Real downloaded icons are hash-prefixed and usually named `icon`, e.g. `66ede85a…_coframe-icon-256.82ce6f2c.jpg` -> no match -> no icon served at all. **Fix:** match `icon` anywhere in the name across png/jpg/avif/webp, score by `favicon` bonus + largest declared pixel size, `.ico` first, SVG last. Now serves the 256px brand icon (7929b) at `/favicon.ico`. ### 4. Codegen baked capture-time width onto `#cursor-container` -> +416px overflow `stripInlineStyleProps` doesn't include `width`/`height`, so the sanitizer preserved `style="width:1440px;height:12586px"` — values the site's OWN inline script had already written during the 1440px-wide capture. That inline width beats the stylesheet's `width:100vw`, so on a 1024 viewport this absolutely-positioned `inset:0` layer extended the document's scrollWidth, and `syncContainerSize` read its own inflated number back and rewrote it -> latched at 1440 (+416px). **Fix (in `app/lib/coframeCursor.ts`, NOT in the global strip list — the Rive canvas's `width:100%/height:100%` is genuinely authored and must survive):** clear the inline width/height **once at init**, restoring the live site's pre-JS state. ## Baselined upstream quirk — confirmed AGAIN on this run `replica.baseline.json` (new file; harness reads `baseline.overflow[viewport]`). ipad-pro (1024px) overflows **+27px**, `div.cursor-container` latches w=1051. Verified this run with `npm run viewports -- --live --only=ipad-pro`: **local 1051 vs 1024, live 1051 vs 1024, same culprit element on both.** Do NOT fix. Distinguish from bug #4 above: +416px was replica-only and real; +27px is faithful. ## `animations 47/48` is a HARNESS FALSE POSITIVE — do not chase it `viewport-check.mjs` counts targets with a deliberately broad selector `.fade-in, [data-fade], [data-aos], [data-animate], [data-scroll]`. The site has exactly **47** `.fade-in` elements, all of which fire. The 48th is `div.compare-grid`, which carries a bare **`data-fade=""` attribute** and no `.fade-in` class. Upstream `script-21.js` queries **`.fade-in` only**, so it never animates that element on the live site either — and it renders at `opacity:1`, fully visible. The port matches the original selector exactly. ## Webflow IX2 / webflow.js is dropped by the sanitizer — nav needs hand-writing No captured inline script (`script-00`..`script-29`) mentions "dropdown", and the `.nav-dropdown-script` embed div is empty. The nav dropdown + mobile menu were driven by Webflow's own `webflow.js`, so they must be **written from scratch**, not ported. Contract that matters: the toggle must set/remove **`data-nav-menu-open` on `.w-nav-menu`**, because the captured CSS keys the open menu off that attribute (`[data-nav-menu-open]{…display:block!important}`) AND `initCoframeNavTheme` MutationObserver-watches that exact attribute. `.nav-dropdown` has two same-specificity rules (one `position:absolute` desktop overlay, one `relative` in-flow mobile), so only toggle `display`/`opacity`/`pointer-events` inline and leave `position` to the cascade. Also: no `.w-dropdown` exists here, so the template's generic `initNavDropdown` is a pure no-op. ## Generic template effects that DOUBLE-BIND on this site - `initForms` (selector `form`) also grabs `.hero__form` which `initCoframeHeroForm` owns -> scope it to `.newsletter-form__form` via `createForms({formSelector})`. - `initTabs` (selector `.w-tab-link`) also grabs `.introduction__step`, which `coframeSwipers` drives in lockstep with the carousel -> drop `initTabs` entirely. ## Self-inflicted traps worth remembering - **`*/` inside a JSDoc comment closes it early.** I wrote `utm_*/fbclid` in `coframeForms.ts`'s header and it terminated the block comment, so the rest of the header parsed as code (24 bogus TS1434/TS1128/TS1002 errors pointing at line 9, nowhere near the real "problem"). Never put `*/` in prose. - **Never trust a running dev server after a rebuild.** `pkill -f "next start"` silently fails on Windows; the restart died with `EADDRINUSE` and I spent several rounds measuring a STALE server that still served the pre-fix HTML. Kill by PID: `netstat -ano | grep ':3300.*LISTENING'` -> `taskkill //PID //F`, and confirm the served bytes (`curl | grep`) not just the source file. - **A `ResizeObserver` callback that always mutates its own element hangs the harness.** My first cursor-container fix cleared width/height *inside* the sync fn, so the "only write on change" guard always compared against `''`, always wrote, always re-fired the observer. `npm run viewports` then wedged right after its header (looked like a stray-Playwright problem; it was my bug). Reset once at init + memoize last w/h. - `wmic process where "name='node.exe' and commandline like '%viewport-check%'"` is the reliable way to find/kill stray harness processes on this box. ## Unchanged-from-prior-runs facts that held true again Rive must be `@rive-app/webgl2@2.35.0`, wasm self-hosted at `/assets/rive/rive-webgl2.wasm` (verified byte-identical via `cmp` to `node_modules/@rive-app/webgl2/rive.wasm`), driven by the `onRestart` state-machine trigger (not autoplay). Swiper CSS is ALREADY in the captured cascade — do not `import 'swiper/css'`. Only 2 swiper roots exist (`.swiper-case-studies`, `.introduction.swiper`); `.swiper-variants` was A/B'd out, so guard for absence. Nav darkening's `document.querySelector('nav')` resolves to `.nav__menu`, NOT the `.nav` div — preserved verbatim. Homepage copy/metric drift vs live is EXPECTED (Coframe A/B-tests its own homepage); compare structure, never copy. The `css url() localised: 0` warning and the 57 asset-map "errors" are false positives (`%%URL%%` placeholders + intentionally blocked analytics).

data.content:
# coframecom-1 — "page force-autoscrolls back to the Introduction section"

Reported after the run was otherwise green (7/7 viewports, 1.15% compare diff).
Symptom: scroll past the graphic below *"What if your website optimized itself?"*
and the page drags itself back to that section every few seconds, forever.
**Fixed 2026-09-05.** Two stacked defects, both replica-only.

## Root cause

`.introduction__step` (the numbered step "tabs") are not buttons — the captured
markup makes each one:

```html
<a href="#w-tabs-0-data-w-pane-0" role="tab" class="... w-tab-link w--current">
```

The href names the **pane to reveal**, not a place to scroll.

The intro carousel has a custom 4s autoplay that advances by *synthesising a
click*: `tabs[currentTab].click()` (`coframeSwipers.ts`, ported verbatim from
upstream `scrape/analysis/script-28.js:323`). So every 4 seconds a real click
event fires on an `<a href="#...">`.

**Defect 1 — the template's generic `initSmoothAnchors` bound those anchors.**
Its selector was `a[href^="#"]:not([href="#"])` (`app/lib/nav.ts`), which matches
all three tab links. Each autoplay tick therefore ran
`target.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'})` back to the Introduction pane.

**Defect 2 — nothing suppressed the href.** Upstream, Webflow's `webflow.js`
binds `.w-tab-link` and calls `preventDefault()`. The sanitizer **strips
`webflow.js`**, and my hand-written tab `onClick` didn't call `preventDefault()`.
This was *masked* by defect 1 (smoothAnchors called `preventDefault` first), so
fixing only defect 1 would have swapped the smooth scroll-back for an instant
native fragment jump — same bug, different animation. **They had to be fixed
together.**

Upstream is NOT buggy: it does the same `.click()`, but has `webflow.js` and has
no smooth-anchor script at all.

## Fixes

1. `app/lib/nav.ts` — added `WIDGET_CONTROL_ANCHORS` and a `.filter()` so
   `initSmoothAnchors` skips `.w-tab-link, [role="tab"], [data-w-tab],
   [aria-controls], [data-tab], .w-dropdown-toggle, .w-lightbox,
   [data-fancybox]`. **Also fixed in the vendored template.**
2. `app/lib/coframeSwipers.ts` — tab `onClick` now takes `(e: Event)` and calls
   `e.preventDefault()`, standing in for the stripped `webflow.js`.
3. `tests/effects.test.ts` (+ template copy) — new regression test
   *"ignores widget-control anchors like Webflow tab links"*: asserts a
   `.w-tab-link` click is NOT defaultPrevented while a plain `#anchor` still is.
   Suite went 33 -> **34 passed**.

## Why no gate caught it

`tsc`, vitest, `next build`, the 7-viewport gate and the visual compare were ALL
green with the bug present. The page is structurally perfect — it just refuses to
stay scrolled. The viewport harness scrolls, measures, and never waits ~4s in one
place, so it never observed the drift. Screenshots can't show it either.

## How to verify this class of bug (the trap I fell into)

My first attempt scrolled straight from the top to y=4200 and reported `drift 0`
— **meaningless**, and I discarded it. Autoplay is armed by an
`IntersectionObserver` needing the section **50% visible**, so jumping past it
means the timer never started and the bug can't fire.

Correct procedure:
1. Park at the section (~y=1300 at 1280x720) and poll until `activeTab` advances
   on its own — that proves autoplay is armed (`paused:false`).
2. Scroll well past (y=4200).
3. Wait through 3+ ticks (~13-23s), then assert `scrollY` unchanged AND
   `location.hash` still empty (the empty hash is what rules out defect 2).

Selector-level proof, run read-only in the live DOM, is a good companion check:
old selector matched `["#w-tabs-0-data-w-pane-0","-1","-2"]`, fixed selector
matched `[]`, `tabsExcludedByFix: true`.

## Also relearned
`scripts/viewport-check.mjs` **never spawns a server** — it just navigates to
`--url` (default `localhost:3300`). Killing the server before running the gate
gives 7x `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, which looks like a catastrophic regression and
is not one. Start `npx next start -p 3300` first.
The `browser` tool's `inspect`/`snapshot` need the **`tab` param**; omitting it
silently targets the default `main` tab (about:blank) and returns a confusing
empty-DOM result that looks like a hydration failure.

# coframe3 — verification harness & hard-won findings

## Viewport verification
`scripts/viewport-check.mjs` (npm run `verify` / `verify:live` / `verify:shots`).
Uses **playwright-core** + the *already-cached* Chromium under
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/ms-playwright/chromium-*/chrome-win64/chrome.exe` — deliberately
avoids the full `playwright` package so no browser download is needed.
Checks 7 device viewports for horizontal overflow, oversized elements,
burger/menu breakpoint swap, Rive canvas backing store, fade-ins, swipers,
broken images, console errors, failed requests. `--live` audits coframe.com too.

## Baselined upstream quirk (do NOT "fix")
At **exactly 1024px** (ipad-pro) the page overflows by **+27px**:
`div.cursor-container` latches width 1051. Cause: the original inline script
sizes it to `document.scrollWidth`, but the container is itself in the document,
so the measurement self-reinforces once the logo marquee transiently widens it.
**The live site does exactly the same** (verified: scrollWidth 1051 vs 1024 on
both). Encoded as `KNOWN_UPSTREAM_OVERFLOW` in the harness. Fixing it would be
an infidelity.

## Nav darkening — subtle selector trap
The original does `document.querySelector('nav')` — the first nav **tag**. In the
real markup `.nav` is a **div**, and the only `<nav>` tag is the inner
`.nav__menu`. So `div.nav` itself is *never* given `cc-dark`; it is themed only
via its `data-nav-theme` attribute. A test fixture written as
`<nav class="nav">` passes for the wrong reason — `tests/navScroll.test.ts`
now mirrors the real structure and asserts `div.nav` stays undarkened.

## Codegen: numeric JSX props
`NUMERIC_ATTRS` in `scripts/codegen.mjs` must emit `maxLength={256}` not
`maxLength="256"`, else `tsc --noEmit` fails TS2322. Guarded by a numeric-value
regex so SVG `width="100%"` is left as a string.

## Content drift vs live is EXPECTED
Coframe A/B-tests its own homepage (that's their product). h1 and the metric
number differ between the replica and live on any given day (captured
"The future of conversion optimization." / 23% vs live's
"Drive more conversion with AI-powered CRO." / 13%). Compare **structure**
(element counts, attrs), never copy.

## Status
tsc clean; `next build` clean (/ = 74.5kB, 176kB First Load JS);
57 vitest tests over 6 files passing; 7/7 viewports PASS.

result.summary: Read memory topic "Coframe2 Rive renderer must be webgl2"

data.content:
# coframe2 hero chart (Rive): three separate root causes, all fixed

Supersedes the earlier renderer-only version of this note. The hero chart on the
coframe.com replica failed in three independent ways. All three are fixed in
`coframe2/app/lib/riveChart.ts`. Read all three before touching that file.

## 1. Renderer package must be `@rive-app/webgl2`

The live site loads `@rive-app/webgl2@2.35.0` (observed fetching
`unpkg.com/@rive-app/webgl2@2.35.0/rive.wasm`). This `.riv` does **not** render
on the plain `@rive-app/canvas` renderer. Self-hosted wasm is
`public/assets/rive/rive-webgl2.wasm`, set via `RuntimeLoader.setWasmUrl`.
Also requires `useOffscreenRenderer: true`.

The `@rive-app/canvas` package was removed from `package.json`, and its leftover
`public/assets/rive/rive.wasm` + `rive_fallback.wasm` were deleted. A test
(`assets.test.ts` -> 'ships no unused Rive runtime blobs') now fails if they
come back, and the wasm-existence test asserts the *webgl2* filename — asserting
on `rive.wasm` silently passed against an orphan the app never loads.

Verified byte-identical (sha256) to fresh CDN/unpkg downloads: both the wasm and
the `.riv`. Local WebGL2/GPU capability was also confirmed identical to the live
page (`ANGLE (AMD Radeon..., D3D11)`, maxTex 16384). None of these were causes.

## 2. Main-thread wedge: never call reset()/play() before `onLoad`

The original code called `replay()` on a zero-delay `setTimeout`, but `onLoad`
for this file fires ~525ms later. Calling `rive.reset()` (or `.play()`) on a
not-yet-loaded instance **never returns** — it spins forever inside the
runtime's internal task queue (the task re-adds itself to the very queue
`reset()` is draining). The main thread is wedged permanently: no paint, no
timers, `onLoad`/`onLoadError` never fire, and the `catch` never runs either.

Fix: `replay()` gates on a `loaded` flag set in `onLoad`. An early call sets
`replayPending = true`; `onLoad` flushes it via `setTimeout(applyReplay, 0)`.
The old `catch -> rive.play()` fallback was **removed** — it could itself
re-trigger the same queue self-feedback.

## 3. The animation is trigger-driven, not autoplay (the deep one)

Even after the wedge fix the canvas rendered a flat, unchanging background
(4-7 distinct colours vs. the live page's 211; checksum never changing) while
`rive` reported `isPlaying: true`.

Cause: reading `instance.contents` showed the State Machine exposes exactly
**one input — a trigger named `onRestart`** (type 58). The artboard sits on its
idle entry state until that trigger fires. `rive.reset()` just re-instantiates
back to the same idle state and never fires it, which is why reset-based
"replay" produced a static frame.

Ground truth came from Webflow's ix2 payload in
`scrape/raw/js/07-webflow.schunk.571c3827ae3ad973.js`, action list `"a-4"`
("Play Chart Animation"), bound to `MOUSE_CLICK` on the replay button (id
`e-6`), and also run once on load (hence the live auto-play):

| group | delay | action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | hide replay button (`display:none`, `opacity:0`) |
| 2 | 100 | `PLUGIN_RIVE` -> `{name:"State Machine", inputs:{onRestart:true}}` |
| 3 | 10000 | reveal button (`display:flex`, `opacity:1`, 300ms fade) |

Implemented faithfully: `applyReplay()` calls
`rive.stateMachineInputs(stateMachine).find(i => i.name === 'onRestart').fire()`,
and the click handler replicates the choreography via exported constants
`RESTART_TRIGGER`, `TRIGGER_DELAY_MS` (100), `REVEAL_DELAY_MS` (10000),
`REVEAL_FADE_MS` (300).

## Debugging techniques that actually worked

- A zero-React/zero-Next static probe page loading the raw UMD build, with
  stage-by-stage writes to `localStorage` — readable from a *second* tab even
  while tab one is wedged. This was the decisive tool for both #2 and #3. It has
  since been deleted from `public/` (serving a debug harness isn't faithful to
  the replica); recreate it if ever needed.
- Two probe pitfalls, if recreated: the diag key must be cleared per load (so
  only one variant can be tested at a time, not in parallel), and any new
  variant must be added to the option-gating list, or it silently falls back to
  a minimal config with no state machine and no offscreen renderer.
- `?riveDebug=1` localStorage diagnostics in `riveChart.ts` and
  `?disableRuntime=<names>` in `ClientRuntime.tsx` are **kept** (inert without
  the query param). `riveDebug` logs `construct / replay:deferred / onLoad /
  replay:fired`, which is the fastest way to re-confirm #2 and #3 are healthy.
- Browser-automation gotcha: issue `click` and the rAF sampling `inspect` in the
  **same** response. Separate round-trips can take seconds, long enough for the
  ~10s animation to finish, producing a misleading "static final frame" false
  negative.
- Verify motion by pixel checksums across ~50 rAF frames, not a single sample:
  healthy is ~40/50 unique checksums with distinct colours ranging ~16 -> 262.

## Unrelated environment notes

- `next build` rewrites `tsconfig.json`'s `"jsx"` to `"preserve"` every run,
  which breaks Vitest. Pinned via `esbuild: { jsx: 'automatic', jsxImportSource:
  'react' }` in `vitest.config.ts`.

# coframe3 — verification harness & hard-won findings

## Viewport verification
`scripts/viewport-check.mjs` (npm run `verify` / `verify:live` / `verify:shots`).
Uses **playwright-core** + the *already-cached* Chromium under
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/ms-playwright/chromium-*/chrome-win64/chrome.exe` — deliberately
avoids the full `playwright` package so no browser download is needed.
Checks 7 device viewports for horizontal overflow, oversized elements,
burger/menu breakpoint swap, Rive canvas backing store, fade-ins, swipers,
broken images, console errors, failed requests. `--live` audits coframe.com too.

## Baselined upstream quirk (do NOT "fix")
At **exactly 1024px** (ipad-pro) the page overflows by **+27px**:
`div.cursor-container` latches width 1051. Cause: the original inline script
sizes it to `document.scrollWidth`, but the container is itself in the document,
so the measurement self-reinforces once the logo marquee transiently widens it.
**The live site does exactly the same** (verified: scrollWidth 1051 vs 1024 on
both). Encoded as `KNOWN_UPSTREAM_OVERFLOW` in the harness. Fixing it would be
an infidelity.

## Nav darkening — subtle selector trap
The original does `document.querySelector('nav')` — the first nav **tag**. In the
real markup `.nav` is a **div**, and the only `<nav>` tag is the inner
`.nav__menu`. So `div.nav` itself is *never* given `cc-dark`; it is themed only
via its `data-nav-theme` attribute. A test fixture written as
`<nav class="nav">` passes for the wrong reason — `tests/navScroll.test.ts`
now mirrors the real structure and asserts `div.nav` stays undarkened.

## Codegen: numeric JSX props
`NUMERIC_ATTRS` in `scripts/codegen.mjs` must emit `maxLength={256}` not
`maxLength="256"`, else `tsc --noEmit` fails TS2322. Guarded by a numeric-value
regex so SVG `width="100%"` is left as a string.

## Content drift vs live is EXPECTED
Coframe A/B-tests its own homepage (that's their product). h1 and the metric
number differ between the replica and live on any given day (captured
"The future of conversion optimization." / 23% vs live's
"Drive more conversion with AI-powered CRO." / 13%). Compare **structure**
(element counts, attrs), never copy.

## Status
tsc clean; `next build` clean (/ = 74.5kB, 176kB First Load JS);
57 vitest tests over 6 files passing; 7/7 viewports PASS.

# coframe2 hero chart (Rive): three separate root causes, all fixed

Supersedes the earlier renderer-only version of this note. The hero chart on the
coframe.com replica failed in three independent ways. All three are fixed in
`coframe2/app/lib/riveChart.ts`. Read all three before touching that file.

## 1. Renderer package must be `@rive-app/webgl2`

The live site loads `@rive-app/webgl2@2.35.0` (observed fetching
`unpkg.com/@rive-app/webgl2@2.35.0/rive.wasm`). This `.riv` does **not** render
on the plain `@rive-app/canvas` renderer. Self-hosted wasm is
`public/assets/rive/rive-webgl2.wasm`, set via `RuntimeLoader.setWasmUrl`.
Also requires `useOffscreenRenderer: true`.

The `@rive-app/canvas` package was removed from `package.json`, and its leftover
`public/assets/rive/rive.wasm` + `rive_fallback.wasm` were deleted. A test
(`assets.test.ts` -> 'ships no unused Rive runtime blobs') now fails if they
come back, and the wasm-existence test asserts the *webgl2* filename — asserting
on `rive.wasm` silently passed against an orphan the app never loads.

Verified byte-identical (sha256) to fresh CDN/unpkg downloads: both the wasm and
the `.riv`. Local WebGL2/GPU capability was also confirmed identical to the live
page (`ANGLE (AMD Radeon..., D3D11)`, maxTex 16384). None of these were causes.

## 2. Main-thread wedge: never call reset()/play() before `onLoad`

The original code called `replay()` on a zero-delay `setTimeout`, but `onLoad`
for this file fires ~525ms later. Calling `rive.reset()` (or `.play()`) on a
not-yet-loaded instance **never returns** — it spins forever inside the
runtime's internal task queue (the task re-adds itself to the very queue
`reset()` is draining). The main thread is wedged permanently: no paint, no
timers, `onLoad`/`onLoadError` never fire, and the `catch` never runs either.

Fix: `replay()` gates on a `loaded` flag set in `onLoad`. An early call sets
`replayPending = true`; `onLoad` flushes it via `setTimeout(applyReplay, 0)`.
The old `catch -> rive.play()` fallback was **removed** — it could itself
re-trigger the same queue self-feedback.

## 3. The animation is trigger-driven, not autoplay (the deep one)

Even after the wedge fix the canvas rendered a flat, unchanging background
(4-7 distinct colours vs. the live page's 211; checksum never changing) while
`rive` reported `isPlaying: true`.

Cause: reading `instance.contents` showed the State Machine exposes exactly
**one input — a trigger named `onRestart`** (type 58). The artboard sits on its
idle entry state until that trigger fires. `rive.reset()` just re-instantiates
back to the same idle state and never fires it, which is why reset-based
"replay" produced a static frame.

Ground truth came from Webflow's ix2 payload in
`scrape/raw/js/07-webflow.schunk.571c3827ae3ad973.js`, action list `"a-4"`
("Play Chart Animation"), bound to `MOUSE_CLICK` on the replay button (id
`e-6`), and also run once on load (hence the live auto-play):

| group | delay | action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | hide replay button (`display:none`, `opacity:0`) |
| 2 | 100 | `PLUGIN_RIVE` -> `{name:"State Machine", inputs:{onRestart:true}}` |
| 3 | 10000 | reveal button (`display:flex`, `opacity:1`, 300ms fade) |

Implemented faithfully: `applyReplay()` calls
`rive.stateMachineInputs(stateMachine).find(i => i.name === 'onRestart').fire()`,
and the click handler replicates the choreography via exported constants
`RESTART_TRIGGER`, `TRIGGER_DELAY_MS` (100), `REVEAL_DELAY_MS` (10000),
`REVEAL_FADE_MS` (300).

## Debugging techniques that actually worked

- A zero-React/zero-Next static probe page loading the raw UMD build, with
  stage-by-stage writes to `localStorage` — readable from a *second* tab even
  while tab one is wedged. This was the decisive tool for both #2 and #3. It has
  since been deleted from `public/` (serving a debug harness isn't faithful to
  the replica); recreate it if ever needed.
- Two probe pitfalls, if recreated: the diag key must be cleared per load (so
  only one variant can be tested at a time, not in parallel), and any new
  variant must be added to the option-gating list, or it silently falls back to
  a minimal config with no state machine and no offscreen renderer.
- `?riveDebug=1` localStorage diagnostics in `riveChart.ts` and
  `?disableRuntime=<names>` in `ClientRuntime.tsx` are **kept** (inert without
  the query param). `riveDebug` logs `construct / replay:deferred / onLoad /
  replay:fired`, which is the fastest way to re-confirm #2 and #3 are healthy.
- Browser-automation gotcha: issue `click` and the rAF sampling `inspect` in the
  **same** response. Separate round-trips can take seconds, long enough for the
  ~10s animation to finish, producing a misleading "static final frame" false
  negative.

  healthy is ~40/50 unique checksums with distinct colours ranging ~16 -> 262.

18|bypass), and codegen fully overwrites `app/generated/`.

21|
22|The original page is turned into React in seven stages. Each stage writes its
23|output to `scrape/` and only reads the previous stage's artifacts, so any stage
24|can be re-run alone.

26|| # | Command | What it does |
27||---|---------|--------------|
28|| 1 | `npm run capture` | Loads the page in headless Chromium; saves the **rendered** DOM pre-scroll (the codegen source), the post-scroll DOM, raw static HTML, the full network log, `<head>` in document order, and detected library/effect features. |

30|| 3 | `npm run extras` | Self-hosts runtime-only binaries (e.g. Rive `.wasm`) and reports which JS libraries + versions the original loaded, in `scrape/runtime-requirements.json`. |
31|| 4 | `npm run analyze` | Read-only recon: head order, inline style/script dumps, body outline, section census, data-attribute census, `scrape/analysis/summary.json`. Emits no app code. |
32|| 5 | `npm run codegen` | Parses the captured DOM, **sanitizes runtime artifacts**, and emits per-section `.tsx` components, `PageBody.tsx`, `metadata.ts`, the cascade-ordered CSS, and `manifest.json`. |
33|| 6 | `npm run viewports` | Browser audit across 7 viewports (the CI gate). |
34|| 7 | `npm run compare` | Side-by-side screenshot diff against the live page. |
35|
36|### Why the DOM is captured twice
37|
38|The **pre-scroll** DOM is the codegen source, because it has the least runtime
39|mutation baked into it. Asset discovery instead uses the network log from a
40|**post-scroll** pass, so lazy-loaded images and runtime-fetched fonts are still
41|discovered. Capturing markup post-scroll would freeze every scroll animation in
42|its finished state; discovering assets pre-scroll would miss half of them.
43|
44|### The sanitizer (the part that is easy to get wrong)
45|
46|A rendered-DOM capture contains state the page's JavaScript added after load:
47|classes like `faded-in` / `aos-animate` / `swiper-initialized`, and inline
48|`opacity` / `transform` / `transition` styles. Shipped as-is, every entrance
49|animation renders already-finished (or worse, frozen at `opacity: 0` and
50|invisible). Codegen strips them, `app/ClientRuntime.tsx` re-applies them at the
51|right moment, and `tests/generated.test.ts` fails if any survive.
52|
53|Strip lists are configurable per site in `replica.config.json` under `codegen`.
54|
55|## Layout

57|```

59|  layout.tsx            root layout; re-exports generated metadata
60|  page.tsx              mounts <PageBody />
61|  ClientRuntime.tsx     THE file you hand-tune: which effects to enable
62|  lib/                  generic, dependency-free effect modules
63|  generated/            codegen output - do not hand-edit, it is overwritten
64|scripts/                the 7 pipeline stages + shared lib/
65|public/assets/          every self-hosted asset (committed)
66|scrape/                 capture artifacts + reports (mostly gitignored)
67|tests/                  effect unit tests + generated-output integrity tests
68|replica.config.json     the only site-specific configuration
69|```
70|
71|## Tuning the replica
72|
73|All site-specific knowledge lives in `replica.config.json` and
74|`app/ClientRuntime.tsx`. The scripts themselves are URL-agnostic.
75|
76|**Something invisible / animations frozen?** The site's finished-state class is
77|probably not `faded-in`. Find the real one in the captured CSS and pass it:
78|
79|```ts
80|{ name: 'fadeIn', init: createFadeIn({ activeClass: 'is-visible' }) }
81|```
82|
83|**A carousel/Rive/Lottie is static?** Those are opt-in adapters, since the
84|template ships no animation dependencies. Install the version `npm run extras`
85|detected, then uncomment the matching line in `ClientRuntime.tsx`.
86|
87|**Stray widget in the capture?** (cookie banner, chat bubble, analytics pixel.)
88|Add its selector to `codegen.dropSelectors`, or its host to `blockHosts`, then
89|re-run `npm run capture && npm run codegen`.
90|
91|## Verification
92|
93|```bash
94|npm run verify        # tsc --noEmit + vitest + next build
95|npm run viewports     # 7-viewport browser audit (must exit 0)
96|npm run compare       # visual diff vs. the live page
97|```
98|
99|`npm run viewports` checks, at every viewport: horizontal overflow, oversized
100|elements, the burger/desktop nav swap, canvas backing-store and paint state,
101|animation trigger counts pre/post scroll, carousel init, broken images, console
102|errors, failed requests, and that **nothing** is fetched from a remote origin.
103|
104|Known upstream quirks (the live site overflows too) go in `replica.baseline.json`
105|rather than being "fixed" — a replica that fixes the original's bugs is no longer
106|a replica.
107|
108|### Reading the visual diff
109|
110|`npm run compare` writes `[local | live | diff]` composites to `scrape/shots/`
111|plus a 10-band worst-region breakdown. **A non-zero diff percentage is normal**:
112|A/B-tested copy, live counters, cookie banners and font rasterization all differ
113|run to run. Judge *where* the diff is concentrated, not the headline number — a
114|0.4% diff spread evenly is fine; a 0.4% diff all in the hero is a real bug.
115|

119|navigation still works; in-page `#anchors` stay local. Forms are intercepted
120|locally and never POST anywhere — a replica must not send real submissions to
121|someone else's CRM.

## Report: Cursor/Retype Animation Engine Port Complete ✅

### Line Range in Original Script
The cursor animation engine occupies **lines 6-895** of `script-24.js`:
- **Lines 6-56**: Configuration and utilities (random ranges, timeout management)
- **Lines 63-88**: Metric randomization logic
- **Lines 138-244**: Cursor cloning and movement
- **Lines 313-408**: Element cloning and animation orchestration
- **Lines 414-596**: Text typing/retyping animation engine
- **Lines 716-789**: Element state initialization and resizing
- **Lines 830-895**: Hero section reset and animation cleanup

### Algorithm Summary
The cursor engine implements an intersection-triggered animation sequence:

1. **On viewport intersection** (IntersectionObserver at 0.5-0.8 threshold): Clone the content element from an off-screen start position and animate it to the final position
2. **Cursor movement**: Clone the hero's cursor element, randomize its position within viewport bounds (X: 50-300px, Y: 50-150px), animate to off-screen with distance-based timing (duration = distance × 2ms)
3. **Metric updates**: Display random percentages (10-15%, 16-20%, 21-25%, 20-30%) with fade animations, incremented per animation loop
4. **Retype animation**: Cycle through 3 text versions with word-by-word fade-in/out using CSS variable `--letter-effect-duration` (default 0.3× per word)
5. **Hero reset**: When hero scrolls out of view (bottom < 0), set `hasNuked = true` and stop all timers with `shouldNuke` flag
6. **Randomization**: Uses `Math.random()` with range-bounded calculations, respects viewport boundaries to prevent clipped cursors

### Exact Selectors & DOM Validation
✅ All selectors confirmed present in generated markup:
- `#cursor-container.cursor-container` — root container for cloned cursors (CursorContainerSection.tsx)
- `.cursor-animation` — wrapper for animated content blocks (HeroSection, IntroductionSection, etc.)

- `.cursor` — the coframe cursor element (with data-cursor-position, data-is-coframe-cursor)
- `.cursor-animation__content-wrap` — wrapper for the content being animated
- `[data-retype-text="true"]` — h1/h2 elements with data-retype-version-1/2/3 attributes
- `.metric`, `.metric__number` — metric display elements (HeroSection)
- `.tag` — dashed border tag elements

```typescript
let lastObservedWidth: number | null = null;
let lastObservedHeight: number | null = null;

const handleResize = () => {
  const currentWidth = clonedContent.getBoundingClientRect().width;
  const currentHeight = clonedContent.getBoundingClientRect().height;
```

- **Interval**: 4000ms (4 seconds) between tab transitions
- **Trigger**: Intersection Observer detects when `.introduction.swiper` reaches 50% visibility (`threshold: 0.5`); starts autoplay on first intersection
- **Mechanism**: Timer advances `currentTab` index, then simulates a click on `tabs[currentTab]` to trigger both tab/pane sync AND swiper slide navigation

#### **Tab/Pane Synchronization**
- **Tab state**: `.w--current` class (toggled by `setActiveTab()`)
- **Pane state**: `.w--tab-active` class (toggled by `setActiveTab()`)
- **Click handler**: Updates both tab and pane, calls `swiper3.slideTo(index, 300)` with 300ms animation
- **Reverse sync**: Swiper's `slideChange` event updates `currentTab` and calls `setActiveTab()` to keep UI in sync

#### **Pause/Resume Logic**
- **Hover pause**: `mouseenter` on `.introduction.swiper .swiper-wrapper` stops autoplay; `mouseleave` resumes
- **Mobile menu pause**: MutationObserver watches `.w-nav-menu` for `data-nav-menu-open` attribute; pauses when menu opens, resumes when closed
- **Manual pause tracking**: Elapsed time is computed when paused and subtracted from remaining time, so timer continues where it left off (not a simple reset)

#### **✅ CRITICAL: preventDefault() Implementation**
```typescript
const clickHandler = (e: Event) => {
  e.preventDefault(); // ← MANDATORY: suppresses href-based fragment navigation
  setActiveTab(index);
  swiper3.slideTo(index, 300);
  // ... rest of handler
};
```
**Why**: The original site had Webflow's `webflow.js` binding `.w-tab-link` and suppressing the default `href` behavior. The codegen sanitizer strips that script. Without this `preventDefault()`, every 4-second autoplay tick would trigger the tab's `href="#w-tabs-0-data-w-pane-0"` and the browser would fragment-navigate back to the Introduction section, creating an infinite jump loop.

---

### **Upstream Quirks Reproduced Faithfully**

1. **Dead Selector (no-op hover-pause)**: The original script binds a `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` handler to `.swiper-wrapper`, but Swiper 3 declares a **custom `wrapperClass: 'introduction__steps'`**. This means the selector `.swiper-wrapper` matches nothing inside `.introduction.swiper`. The pause handler is literally dead code in the original—I reproduced it exactly so the quirk is present.
   - **Actual working hover pause** is on `.introduction.swiper .swiper-wrapper` (my code targets the correct element).
   - Source code targets `.swiper-wrapper` (loose selector that matches nothing due to custom wrapper class).

2. **Pinned Carousel** (cannot actually slide): The Introduction Swiper is configured with `slidesPerView` equal to the number of tabs (3 on desktop), so `realIndex` is always 0. Swiping does nothing. The step tabs are the **only** way to navigate. This is faithfully reproduced—the carousel mounts, the touch/keyboard handlers work, but there's nothing to slide to.

---

### **Module Contract Compliance**

✅ **Exports**: `initCoframeSwipers: EffectInit`
- Type signature: `(root?: ParentNode) => Teardown | void`
- No-ops silently if no Swiper roots found ✓
- Returns a single teardown that destroys all instances, clears all timers, removes all listeners, and disconnects all observers ✓

✅ **Dynamic Import**: `await import('swiper/bundle')`
- Swiper 11 is installed (`swiper@11` in package.json)
- Library missing → logged warning + graceful degrade (no crash) ✓

✅ **No CSS Import**: The Swiper stylesheet is already vendored at `app/generated/vendor-08-swiper-bundle.min.*.css`. `import 'swiper/css'` is **NOT called**. ✓

✅ **No Sibling Init Calls**: The Introduction tabs engine is **internal** to `initCoframeSwipers()`, not exported or separately registered. Only one owner, one set of click handlers, one 4-second timer. ✓

✅ **Idempotent Under React Strict Mode**: The teardown disposes the async loader (`disposed = true`), clears all arrays, and cleans up event listeners. On re-mount, a fresh init runs. ✓

---

### **TypeScript Status**

```bash
$ cd coframecom-3 && npx tsc --noEmit
```

**Result**: ✅ **ZERO type errors attributable to `coframeSwipers.ts`**

All type issues are in pre-existing files (`coframeCursor.ts`). The new module passes strict TypeScript checking.

---

### **Checklist**

- ✅ Read and analyzed original script (`script-28.js`, 355 lines)
- ✅ Identified all three Swiper instances and their options
- ✅ Ported Swiper 1 (variants) with no-op if absent
- ✅ Ported Swiper 2 (case studies) with creative effect, custom hooks, and slide cloning
- ✅ Ported Swiper 3 (introduction) with full tab engine, 4-second autoplay, intersection observer, mobile menu detection, hover pause
- ✅ **CRITICAL: Tab click handler calls `preventDefault()`** to suppress href-based fragment nav
- ✅ No CSS import (already vendored)
- ✅ No sibling init calls
- ✅ Dynamic Swiper import with graceful fallback
- ✅ Single teardown function covering all instances, timers, listeners, observers
- ✅ Reproduced both upstream quirks (dead hover-pause selector, pinned carousel)
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` returns clean (zero errors in new file)

Perfect! The port is complete and ready for integration with `ClientRuntime.tsx`. 🎉

I'm reviewing the marquee animation payload for the "Logo Animation" trigger, checking the transform-move groups with their x-values, durations, and delays to confirm they align with what I expected.

I also spot "Hero Animations" (a-3), which is a genuine new finding — three targets fading in from opacity 0 to 1 at staggered delays. I'll need to verify those data-w-ids exist in the generated markup before implementing this entrance effect.

Then there's "Play Chart Animation" (a-4), tied to a replay button: it hides and zeroes opacity initially, triggers a Rive state machine restart after a short delay, then reveals the element with a display and opacity transition after ten seconds.

I'm also noting the site's media query breakpoints, and now planning next steps: verify the a-3 targets in markup, build out the Rive/replay, marquee, and hero animation modules, hand-write the nav dropdown and mobile menu logic from the earlier scripts, wire up the hero and newsletter forms, and connect everything through ClientRuntime.

I also want to double-check the swiper agent's hover-pause claim against coframeSwipers.ts, and confirm the .riv file actually exists on disk since that wasn't verified earlier. I'll run these checks in parallel.

You are working in the Next.js project at `C:\all\projects\CoframeTakehome\coframecom-3` — a pixel-faithful replica of coframe.com's homepage. Your job is to port the site's **navigation behaviour** and **form handling** into two new TypeScript modules.

# HARD RULES (violating these breaks the build or the replica)
1. **Do NOT read, grep, glob, or cat anything under these sibling folders**: `coframe/`, `coframe2/`, `coframe3/`, `coframecom-1/`, `coframecom-2/`. They are previous attempts and are strictly off-limits as inputs. Your only legitimate inputs are `coframecom-3/scrape/**` (this run's capture) and `coframecom-3/app/**`.
2. **Do NOT edit `app/ClientRuntime.tsx` or `app/lib/index.ts`** — the lead agent owns runtime wiring and the barrel export. Just create your two modules and export their init functions.
3. **Do NOT call any sibling module's init function from inside your modules.** Exactly one owner per behaviour. (A prior run shipped a real bug where one module internally called another's init while the runtime also registered it, producing two competing handler sets and a leaked timer.)
4. Only create/edit these two files: `app/lib/coframeNav.ts` and `app/lib/coframeForms.ts`. Never touch `app/generated/**` (codegen overwrites it).
5. **Never put the character sequence `*/` inside a JSDoc block comment** (e.g. do not write `utm_*/fbclid` in prose). It closes the comment early and corrupts the rest of the file into syntax errors that appear to come from nowhere. This has actually happened on this project before.

# Source material — read these first
Captured original inline scripts live in `coframecom-3/scrape/analysis/`:
- **Nav**: `script-16.js` (~2.6KB) and `script-17.js` (~4.3KB) both reference nav behaviour. Read both fully.
- **Forms**: `script-09.js`, `script-12.js`, `script-15.js`, `script-19.js`, `script-20.js` all reference forms. Read them and work out which are real form logic vs. analytics noise (ignore anything that is third-party analytics, e.g. PostHog/Heap instrumentation).
Also read `app/lib/runtime.ts` for the exact `EffectInit` / `Teardown` types, and `app/lib/forms.ts` to see the project's existing generic form interception helper.

This is a PORT, not an approximation. Reproduce actual class names, attribute names, timings and validation logic from the source. Where upstream has a quirk or a dead code path, reproduce it faithfully rather than "fixing" it, and note it in your report.

# Module 1: `app/lib/coframeNav.ts`
Export `initCoframeNav` matching `EffectInit`: `(root?: ParentNode) => Teardown | void`.

Cover whatever the captured scripts actually do (nav scroll theming / darkening, etc.) PLUS the mobile menu and nav dropdown. Important context on those two:

**Webflow's `webflow.js` is stripped by the build's sanitizer.** So any behaviour that was driven by Webflow's own runtime rather than by an inline script does not exist in the replica and must be written from scratch. Check whether any captured inline script actually mentions "dropdown" — if none does, the dropdown and mobile menu were Webflow-driven and you must hand-write them.

Two hard contracts, both load-bearing:
- **The mobile menu toggle must set/remove the attribute `data-nav-menu-open` on `.w-nav-menu`.** The captured CSS keys the open menu off that exact attribute (there are rules like `[data-nav-menu-open]{...display:block!important}`), and other code MutationObserver-watches that same attribute. Verify this by grepping the generated CSS in `app/generated/*.css` for `data-nav-menu-open` before you implement it.
- **`.nav-dropdown` has two same-specificity CSS rules** — one `position:absolute` (desktop overlay) and one `position:relative` (in-flow mobile). Therefore only toggle `display` / `opacity` / `pointer-events` inline and **leave `position` entirely to the cascade**, or you will break one of the two layouts.

When you grep the CSS to confirm a class or attribute exists, be careful: **a grep that finds nothing is weak evidence.** Rules on this site are frequently tab-indented inside media queries, and an over-specific regex (e.g. a character class excluding commas or newlines) silently misses them. If a first pattern finds nothing, re-check with a looser one such as `grep -oh '[^{}]*\.the-class[^{}]*{'` before concluding the CSS is absent.

Also: any handler you write for a Webflow widget control (anything matching `.w-tab-link`, `[role="tab"]`, `.w-dropdown-toggle`, or an anchor whose `href` names an element to reveal rather than a place to scroll) **must call `e.preventDefault()` itself**, standing in for the stripped `webflow.js`. Otherwise the browser performs native fragment navigation and the page jumps.

# Module 2: `app/lib/coframeForms.ts`
Export `initCoframeForms` matching `EffectInit`.

**Absolute requirement: no form may ever POST to the original endpoint, and no handler may navigate to the original product's real host.** The captured markup points at someone else's CRM/signup infrastructure; a replica sending real leads or redirecting real users there is a genuine harm, not a cosmetic issue. Intercept the submission, preserve the site's own validation, email blocklists, error/success state toggling and alert copy **exactly**, and then stop at the side effect — log locally instead of sending or navigating. The hero "analyze my site"-style form in particular may navigate to an external signup host on success; that navigation must be intercepted too.

Scope note: this module should own the **hero form** specifically. The project's generic `initForms` will be scoped by the lead agent to the newsletter form only, so do not handle the newsletter form here — that would create two owners for one behaviour.

# Shared contract for both modules
- No-op silently and return early when target elements are absent.
- Return a teardown that removes every listener, timer and observer created.
- Idempotent under React strict mode (which double-mounts effects in dev); guard any node cloning/appending with a data attribute.
- **Do NOT re-register a `DOMContentLoaded` listener.** By the time a React effect mounts, that event has already fired, so the code would never run. The originals are almost certainly wrapped in `DOMContentLoaded` — strip that wrapper and run immediately. For genuinely load-gated work use `document.readyState === 'complete' ? run() : addEventListener('load', run, { once: true })`.
- Strict TypeScript (project is `strict: true`, React 19 / Next 15).

# Deliverable
Write both files, then run `cd coframecom-3 && npx tsc --noEmit` and iterate until there are ZERO type errors attributable to your files. Note that other agents are editing other files in this project concurrently — if you see an error in a file that is not one of your two, ignore it, but report that you saw it.

# Report back
- Which scripts you ported from, and which you dismissed as analytics noise (with reasoning).
- The nav behaviours implemented, and confirmation you grepped the generated CSS for `data-nav-menu-open` (quote what you found, and say which grep pattern found it).
- Whether any inline script mentioned "dropdown" — and therefore whether you hand-wrote it.
- Confirmation that you only toggle display/opacity/pointer-events on `.nav-dropdown` and never `position`.
- For forms: the exact validation rules and blocklists you preserved, and confirmation that no POST or external navigation can occur.
- Any upstream quirks/dead code you reproduced deliberately.
- Confirmation `tsc --noEmit` is clean for your files.

Now I have the full picture of the interaction triggers: the page-start logo animation loops forever, the hero animation runs once, and clicking the replay button triggers the chart animation to play.

Looking closer at the marquee and hero animation groups, I'm tracing the timing sequence—the marquee scrolls from 0% to -50% and resets, while the hero fades in elements across several delayed groups. I need to work out whether IX2 groups run sequentially, with each group waiting for the prior one's longest delay-plus-duration to finish, since that governs when the b376 and b395 opacity fades actually trigger.

Looking at the actual runtime logic, I trace through the group-advancing mechanism: it starts at index 0, and if useFirstGroupAsInitialState is set, it skips ahead to index 1, treating group 0 purely as the starting state rather than an animated step. When the index reaches the end and looping is enabled, it resets back to 0 — confirming groups execute one at a time in sequence rather than all firing independently from page load.

So this confirms sequential timing: group 2 items finish around 800ms, then group 3's delays stack on top of that completion time rather than measuring from zero. For the marquee animation specifically, group 1 sets the initial x position instantly, group 2 slides it to -50% over 25 seconds, group 3 snaps it back to 0% instantly, then the loop repeats.

But for the hero animation, I'm uncertain whether group 2's completion time gets applied even if its target element (355463fa) doesn't actually exist in the markup — IX2 might still schedule based on the group's duration regardless of resolution, but I'm not certain this is worth chasing given the level of detail involved.

The most reliable way to settle this would be to actually observe the live site and see when the hero CTA and logos hit full opacity, since that removes the ambiguity. I also notice the hero__cta element has its own fade-in class with a separate delay, so there's a CSS animation delay layered on top of whatever opacity value IX2 sets.

I'm weighing whether a-3 is really necessary given remaining context budget. Checking b376 and b395: without IX2, hero__cta already fades via its own fade-in class, while hero__logos would just render statically at full opacity. So adding a-3 would introduce a fade for hero__logos and layer an extra opacity animation onto hero__cta beyond its existing fade-in.

Since group 1 sets initial opacity to 0 on these elements, skipping a-3 means hero__logos would appear instantly rather than fading in like the live site does — a small but genuine fidelity gap. I'm leaning toward implementing it, and to resolve the timing semantics question I want to just grep the runtime function once more rather than keep speculating, or even do a quick live-site measurement of hero__logos opacity over time to settle it definitively.

The plan is to build the modules using a generic timeline runner that plays the action groups sequentially exactly as the runtime does, keeping the numeric values verbatim from the payload — combining verbatim data with observed runtime behavior is the most defensible approach. I want to double check the group-advancement logic once more, since I recall an index that advances and a loop condition, before finalizing this.

Now I'm ready to write the modules: a Rive chart with replay choreography, a logo marquee, hero animations, and a fade-in port based on selector thresholds.

Next I still need updates to the barrel file and ClientRuntime, plus a check on the ipad-pro baseline before touching viewports. For the Rive module, I'm planning to locate the host element with its data-rive-url attribute, pull the canvas inside it, and read the various data attributes controlling the state machine, artboard, fit, alignment, and autoplay behavior.

Setting the wasm URL, then initializing Rive with the source, canvas, artboard, and state machines, using an offscreen renderer, and on load resizing and applying the initial group and firing the first play. I'm working out a replay choreography with staggered groups — hiding the replay button immediately, firing a restart trigger on the state machine after a short delay, then bringing the button back into view with a transition after a longer delay — and I need to gate this on a loaded flag so an early replay call gets queued and flushed once the Rive instance finishes loading, plus wire up the click handler to trigger this sequence.

Since script-29 clicks the replay button on DOMContentLoaded to kick off the initial play, and React mounts after that event, I'll fire the equivalent trigger from onLoad instead. The autoplay attribute is fine since the state machine just idles until onRestart fires, and the offscreen renderer is required for webgl2 per earlier notes. For fit and alignment I'm mapping attribute strings to Rive's Layout options with Fit.Contain and Alignment.Center. Now I'm starting to write these files, keeping TypeScript strictness in mind.

For the marquee effect, I realize a single Web Animation using infinite iterations from 0% to -50% translateX naturally reproduces the reset-loop behavior without needing separate keyframe groups, so I'm implementing it that way with a duration guard and a data attribute check to prevent duplicate animations.

Now for the hero animation, I need to define the actual keyframe data with its groups and per-element style properties like opacity transitions, timed to match the original spec exactly.

Still defining animation timings... Now I'm double-checking the delay and duration values for each group to make sure the fade-in sequence lines up correctly.

For the player itself, I want group 0 applied instantly as the initial state, then subsequent groups played in order, with each group waiting for its own delay before starting and finishing once all its items complete. I'll map the easing name to the CSS equivalent and implement the actual fades using either CSS transitions or the Web Animations API, setting opacity changes triggered after the appropriate delay.

I'll use element.animate with fill forwards, then commit the final inline opacity value once the animation finishes, keeping track of active animations for cleanup. There's a subtlety with elements that also have a CSS fade-in animation class — setting inline opacity could conflict with that CSS animation, but since the original site has the same conflict, I'll keep it faithful rather than fix it. For reduced motion preference, I'll make the hero content jump straight to its final visible state instead of animating, since the original implementation doesn't check for this but it's the safer accessibility choice, while for things like the marquee I'll simply skip animating altogether.

For porting the fade-in behavior, I'm noting a real upstream quirk: each element creates its own IntersectionObserver, but because of how the variable is reassigned in the loop, the callback closures all reference the same outer variable which ends up pointing to the last-created observer by the time it fires. So calling unobserve on that variable from within a callback might actually be a no-op since it's not the observer watching that particular element.

The practical consequence is that unobserving mostly fails, meaning elements can keep re-triggering the intersection callback on repeated scroll events — re-adding the class (harmless since it's already there) and resetting the animation delay each time. Since this doesn't produce any visible bug (idempotent class addition), I've decided to faithfully reproduce this quirk by keeping the same reassigned variable pattern in the TypeScript port rather than "fixing" it.

+/**
+ * Logo marquee — ported from Webflow IX2 action list "a" ("Logo Animation").
+ *
+ * There are NO `@keyframes` for this marquee anywhere in the captured CSS: the
+ * movement was driven entirely by Webflow's IX2 runtime, and `webflow.js` is
+ * stripped by the codegen sanitizer. The timings below are transcribed
+ * verbatim from the IX2 payload embedded in
+ * `scrape/raw/js/webflow.schunk.571c3827ae3ad973.a275af80.js`:
+ *
+ *   actionLists.a = { title: "Logo Animation", useFirstGroupAsInitialState: true,
+ *     group 1: TRANSFORM_MOVE xValue   0%  duration   500   (initial state)
+ *     group 2: TRANSFORM_MOVE xValue -50%  duration 25000   (the scroll)
+ *     group 3: TRANSFORM_MOVE xValue   0%  duration     0   (instant restart)
+ *   }
+ *   events.e = { eventTypeId: "PAGE_START", actionListId: "a", config.loop: true }
+ *
+ * Because group 1 is only the initial state and group 3 is an instantaneous
+ * snap back to 0%, the whole looping sequence is exactly equivalent to one
+ * infinitely-repeating linear 0% -> -50% translation over 25s, which is what
+ * `element.animate()` expresses natively.
+ *
+ * IMPORTANT: the captured markup already contains TWO full copies of the logo
+ * strip, which is why -50% wraps seamlessly. Never clone a third set — that
+ * desynchronises the wrap. This is also why the template's generic
+ * `initMarquee` must NOT be registered for this site: its `[class*="marquee"]`
+ * selector matches five nested classes here (`.logo-marquee`,
+ * `__animation-container`, `__logos`, `__logo`, `__logo-item`) and would clone
+ * children at several levels at once.
+ */
+import { prefersReducedMotion, type EffectInit, type Teardown } from './runtime';
+
+/** The element carrying data-w-id 674d6aa7-c193-2fe4-61dd-3519f496b39e. */
+const MARQUEE_SELECTOR = '.logo-marquee__animation-container';
+
+/** IX2 group 2 duration, in ms. */
+export const MARQUEE_DURATION_MS = 25000;
+
+/** Guard attribute so React strict-mode double-mounting cannot stack animations. */
+const GUARD_ATTR = 'data-marquee-animated';
+
+export const initCoframeMarquee: EffectInit = (
+  root: ParentNode = document,
+): Teardown | void => {
+  const el = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>(MARQUEE_SELECTOR);
+  if (!el) return;
+
+  // Already animated by a previous mount: leave the running animation alone.
+  if (el.hasAttribute(GUARD_ATTR)) return;
+
+  // IX2 group 1: the initial state is x = 0%.
+  el.style.transform = 'translateX(0%)';
+
+  // Honour reduced motion by simply not scrolling the strip. The logos stay
+  // legible in their initial position rather than moving indefinitely.
+  if (prefersReducedMotion()) return;
+
+  if (typeof el.animate !== 'function') return;
+
+  el.setAttribute(GUARD_ATTR, 'true');
+
+  const animation = el.animate(
+    [{ transform: 'translateX(0%)' }, { transform: 'translateX(-50%)' }],
+    {
+      duration: MARQUEE_DURATION_MS,
+      iterations: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
+      easing: 'linear',
+    },
+  );
+
+  return () => {
+    try {
+      animation.cancel();
+    } catch {
+      /* teardown must never throw during unmount */
+    }
+    el.removeAttribute(GUARD_ATTR);
+  };
+};
