blocks.text: The comparison run finished with an average pixel difference of 0.82% across 7 viewports, and all heights matched exactly between local and live — a strong signal. Now I need to actually look at the composites per the verification gate, starting with the worst offenders: ipad-mini at 1.626%, laptop at 1.321%, and desktop-wide at 0.895%. I also still need to run the autoscroll regression check for the known bug where the page force-scrolls back to the Introduction section, using the browser tool for that.

Average **0.82%** pixel difference, and notably **local height == live height exactly at all 7 viewports** (12383/12383, 13200/13200, 12586/12586, …) — a strong layout-fidelity signal. Now I must actually look at the composites rather than trust the numbers.

The iPad-mini composite looks great, with the layout pixel-aligned across nav, hero, form, and chart sections. The differing numbers ($367,475 vs $241,890, 19.8% vs 17.3%) are just from the Rive chart animating between capture frames, not layout bugs.

I notice local shows three variant cards while live shows only two — likely another animation timing difference where the cards appear progressively as the chart animates, rather than an actual missing element. It's possible these variant cards render as part of the Rive canvas itself rather than as separate DOM elements, which would explain why the count differs by capture moment.

Actually, checking the canvas dimensions (697x533 backing at ipad-pro), it seems too small to contain the whole card — it's probably just rendering the line chart, not the variant cards. Since local shows a higher dollar value and conversion rate than live, it makes sense that local's animation had progressed further, revealing an extra variant card along with it. There's also a floating "Ask ChatGPT about us" widget visible in local's bottom-right that doesn't appear in the same spot in live, flagged in the diff.

I'm thinking this widget is likely part of the statically captured markup (server-rendered by Coframe) rather than a stripped third-party script, so it's rendering faithfully as captured even if live shows it differently timed. I want to check the other composite screenshots — laptop and desktop-wide — along with the 90-100% similarity band.

The worst-diff band at 90-100% is consistently the bottom of the fold area, which lines up with the variant cards and this widget region across viewports, so that's consistent with what I already found. I'll now read the laptop composite (worst desktop diff at 1.32%) and desktop-wide, and also run an autoscroll regression check with the browser tool.

The ipad-mini composite is genuinely excellent — every layout landmark is pixel-aligned (nav, headline wrap, subcopy, URL field, caption, chart card, variant cards). The red diff is confined to:

- **Chart counter values** (`$367,475` vs `$241,890`, `19.8%` vs `17.3%`) and the plotted lines → Rive animation frame timing, and consistently *self-consistent*: local shows a higher count **and** one more revealed variant card (3 vs 2), i.e. local was simply further along the same animation.
- **A floating "Ask ChatGPT about us" widget** present locally at bottom-right.

That last one I want to be sure about. Let me check the two desktop composites and confirm the widget's origin.

The laptop composite looks great — local and live both show identical stats ($367,475/19.8%, 3 variant cards). The only difference is the logo marquee being at different scroll phases since it's an infinite animation, accounting for that 4.77% diff band. I also notice the "Ask ChatGPT about us" widget appears in both versions, confirming it's part of the captured markup.

For ipad-mini, the widget shows in local but live's screenshot got cut off before that area was visible, so that's a minor false positive rather than a real discrepancy. Next I want to quickly check desktop-wide and then run the autoscroll regression check in the browser.

Both remaining composites I've inspected look good, and the worst bands consistently show up in the 90-100% region on mobile, which lines up with the marquee-phase explanation since that's where the logo marquee sits above the fold. I'll confirm this by checking the iphone-14-pro composite next, then move to the actual functional check—verifying the autoscroll regression bug in the browser—since that's the more important remaining verification.

Since this is the final verification gate, thoroughness matters more than efficiency, so I'll check both images.

The laptop composite is even stronger — and it resolves the widget question: **local and live *both* render the "Ask ChatGPT about us" widget**, so it's genuinely part of the page, not something I failed to strip. Here local and live also both show `$367,475 / 19.8%` and all 3 variant cards (identical). The 60-70% band (4.77%) is the **logo marquee caught at a different animation phase** — REUTERS/OpenAI/Inc./The Economist are offset horizontally, exactly as an infinite 25s loop must be.

Let me confirm the mobile 90-100% band is that same marquee, and validate the widest breakpoint.

For the iphone-14-pro composite, local shows fully rendered data with charts and variant cards, while live still shows an empty zero-state chart since its animation hadn't started yet — meaning local is actually further along, which is good evidence the Rive chart port is working correctly. So all the diffs I'm seeing are just animation-phase timing differences rather than real content issues.

Now I want to verify the known autoscroll regression bug where the page force-jumps back to the Introduction section due to tab anchor hijacking. I'm considering whether to check this live by scrolling and measuring scrollY over time, or statically by inspecting whether any anchor handlers call preventDefault or reference pane hrefs — since scrolling itself is a mutating action that may need approval.

I'll be efficient: first open and navigate to the page read-only, then inspect for suspicious anchor/tab-link elements and their hrefs along with the current scrollY, and also check console errors, before proceeding to the mutating scroll test to confirm scroll position stability.

The iphone-14-pro composite is the clearest evidence yet that the **Rive chart genuinely works**: local renders `$367,475 / 19.8%` with plotted lines and 3 variant cards, while **live** was still at `$0 / 0%` with an empty chart — my replica was *ahead* in the same animation, not missing it. Text and layout are pixel-aligned line-for-line.

All diffs across all 7 composites are animation-phase or A/B content, never layout or assets. Now the important functional check: the autoscroll regression, which matters because I deliberately kept `initSmoothAnchors` registered.

I want to check for the autoscroll regression bug—clicking a tab link or an anchor whose href names a pane rather than a scroll target seems to force the page to autoscroll. I recall `initSmoothAnchors` had some "widget-anchor exclusion fix," so I should inspect the DOM read-only for hash-href anchors and `.w-tab-link` elements to confirm.
Page loaded. Now inspecting (read-only) for the exact element class that caused the prior run's forced-autoscroll bug: anchors/tab-links whose href names a pane rather than a scroll target.

The DOM inspection reveals a much smaller risk surface this time: only one bare `href="#"` on the newsletter button, which could trigger an autoscroll-to-top since its target doesn't exist, while the three tab-link elements have no href at all so they pose no navigation hazard.

That means the prior run's tab anchor hijack bug can't recur here. But I want to check how `initSmoothAnchors` handles bare `#` hrefs, and I've realized something more significant — since `.newsletter-form__button` is actually an `<a>` element rather than a real submit button, my form-binding logic targeting `.newsletter-form__form` submit events might never fire when someone clicks it, meaning the button click could just jump to the anchor and do nothing else.

I want to check whether any captured analytics script already handles the newsletter button click, and also read through the smooth-anchor logic to confirm the `href="#"` scroll-jump risk I flagged in item 7 is real.

Key finding from the DOM: the prior run's bug **cannot recur here** — all 3 `.w-tab-link` elements have `href: null`, so there's no anchor to hijack. But this surfaced a *different* real hazard: exactly one hash anchor, `href="#"` on `.newsletter-form__button`, whose target does **not** exist. A bare `#` click jumps the page to top.

Let me check whether `initSmoothAnchors` neutralizes that, and how upstream handled this button.

I'm confirming that initSmoothAnchors deliberately skips bare `href="#"` links, so the newsletter button isn't affected by that module—meaning the default browser jump-to-top behavior would apply unless another script intercepts it, and I recall script-20.js handles the newsletter form separately.

The newsletter button is an anchor tag, not a submit button, so my generic createForms submit-listener approach won't catch its click at all—it'll just navigate to `#` and jump to the page top, doing nothing for the form. This is a real bug I need to fix by porting script-20.js's dedicated click handler instead of relying on the generic form initializer, so I should read that file in full.

Two important findings, and one is a **real bug I need to fix**:

1. `initSmoothAnchors` uses `a[href^="#"]:not([href="#"])` — it deliberately excludes bare `#`, so it is *not* the autoscroll culprit. Good.
2. **But that means nothing suppresses the browser's default jump-to-top**, and `script-20.js` proves upstream had a *dedicated* newsletter handler binding `.newsletter-form__button` — which is an `<a href="#">`, **not** a submit button. My generic `createForms` binds the `submit` event, which that anchor will never fire. So the newsletter form currently does nothing *and* jumps the page to top.

Script-20 reveals the actual bug: the upstream code binds a click handler on the newsletter button anchor, prevents default, validates the email, then calls requestSubmit on the form, plus handles Enter key separately. My generic form wiring only binds a submit listener, so clicking the anchor never triggers submit and just jumps to the page anchor instead.

The fix is to build a dedicated newsletter module that faithfully replicates that behavior — click on the button validates and calls requestSubmit or alerts, Enter key on the form does the same — while keeping the generic form handler in place to intercept the resulting submit event locally so nothing actually posts. That keeps validation and submit-interception cleanly separated without either mechanism fighting over the same event.

Since requestSubmit dispatches a cancelable submit event, the generic handler will still catch and preventDefault it properly. I want to scope the selector to `.footer .newsletter-form__form` to match upstream, with a fallback to the bare selector in case `.footer` isn't present. The alert() behavior is intrusive but matches the original, so I'll keep it faithful. Now I'm writing the coframeNewsletter module itself before rewiring it in and rerunning tsc plus the scroll regression test.

`script-20.js` confirms a **real regression in my wiring**: upstream bound a `click` handler on `.newsletter-form__button` that calls `preventDefault()`, validates, then `form.requestSubmit()`. My generic `createForms` only listens for `submit` — which an `<a href="#">` never fires. So right now the newsletter button would jump the page to top and do nothing. Fixing it with a faithful port.

Checking the DOM confirms the bug: the button is an anchor tag, not a submit button, so the generic form binding that listens for submit events never fires on click. I'll port the newsletter script faithfully into its own module and rewire the client runtime to keep the generic form handler for submit interception while adding a dedicated click/Enter handler that calls requestSubmit() to trigger the cancelable submit event properly.

DOM confirms the bug precisely: `hasSubmitButton: false`, `buttonTag: "A"`, `buttonHref: "#"`, `method: "post"` with no action. A click on that anchor fires no `submit` event, so my generic handler never runs — the page would just jump to top. Writing the faithful port of `script-20.js`.
Now wiring it in — barrel export plus registering it ahead of the interception layer.

--- a/coframecom-3/app/lib/index.ts
+++ b/coframecom-3/app/lib/index.ts
@@ -11,6 +11,7 @@
 export * from './coframeSwipers';
 export * from './coframeNav';
 export * from './coframeForms';
+export * from './coframeNewsletter';
 export * from './coframeFadeIn';
 export * from './coframeMarquee';
 export * from './coframeHeroAnim';

--- a/coframecom-3/app/ClientRuntime.tsx
+++ b/coframecom-3/app/ClientRuntime.tsx
@@ -29,6 +29,7 @@
   initCoframeHeroAnim,
   initCoframeMarquee,
   initCoframeNav,
+  initCoframeNewsletter,
   initCoframeSwipers,
   createCoframeRive,
   initCounters,
@@ -79,9 +80,19 @@
   // submission locally instead of navigating to start.coframe.com.
   { name: 'coframeForms', init: initCoframeForms },
 
+  // Newsletter validation + submit triggering (script-20.js). Required because
+  // `.newsletter-form__button` is an <a href="#">, not a submit control: no
+  // `submit` event is ever fired by clicking it, and the bare `#` would
+  // otherwise jump the page to the top. Must be registered BEFORE the generic
+  // interception effect below, which catches the submit this one triggers.
+  { name: 'coframeNewsletter', init: initCoframeNewsletter },
+
   // --- generic effects, kept -------------------------------------------------
-  // Newsletter form only. Scoped deliberately: the hero form is owned by
-  // `coframeForms` above, and two submit handlers on one form would double-fire.
+  // Newsletter form only, and only as the *interception* layer: it cancels the
+  // submit that `coframeNewsletter` triggers so nothing is POSTed anywhere, and
+  // reveals the site's own `.w-form-done` block. Scoped deliberately — the hero
+  // form is owned by `coframeForms`, and two submit handlers on one form would
+  // double-fire.
   { name: 'newsletterForm', init: createForms({ formSelector: '.newsletter-form__form' }) },
   { name: 'smoothAnchors', init: initSmoothAnchors },
   { name: 'accordion', init: initAccordion },

args.content:
# coframecom-3 — 6th coframe.com replica run (port 3302)

Slug `coframecom-3` (coframecom, -1/-2 taken). Port 3302 (3300/3301 taken).
`targetUrl` = `https://www.coframe.com/` (resolved form, NOT the given
`http://www.` form) so asset-map hostnames match what the browser requests.

## Final state: all 8 checklist items green
- `npm run verify` exit 0 — tsc clean, vitest 34/34, next build 4/4 static pages.
- `npm run viewports` — PASS, 0 problems / 7 viewports. canvas painted=true at
  all 7, carousels 2 initialised, 119 imgs 0 broken, real font loaded.
- `npm run compare` — avg **0.82%** diff over 7 viewports, and **local page
  height == live page height exactly at all 7** (12383/12383, 13200/13200,
  12586/12586, ...). All residual diff is Rive-frame phase, marquee phase, or
  Coframe's own A/B copy. No layout or asset drift.

## captureMode: static was the right call again
Verified ratio 0.82 (1176/1439 elements). Avoids baking in runtime-generated
duplicate nodes (cursor clones, split hero letters) that caused the
coframecom-2 "duplicated elements" bug. Belt-and-braces in replica.config.json:
`emptySelectors: [".cursor-container"]`, `unwrapSelectors: [".letter-effect"]`.

## Template bug found & fixed this run (also fixed in vendored template)
`scripts/codegen.mjs` hardcoded `manifest.source` to the "rendered" string
regardless of the actual `markupSource` used, so manifest.json lied whenever
captureMode was static. Fixed in BOTH `coframecom-3/scripts/codegen.mjs` and
`~/.klenny/skills/website-replica/template/scripts/codegen.mjs`.
The 4 previously-known template bugs were already fixed in the vendored copy.

## Webflow IX2 extraction — the big win, reusable
`webflow.js` is stripped by the sanitizer, so ALL IX2 motion is lost unless
ported. Extracted the real payload out of the minified
`scrape/raw/js/webflow.schunk.571c3827ae3ad973.a275af80.js` with node (find
`actionLists:{a:{id:"a"`, then `lastIndexOf("events:{")` before it). Full map:

| Event | Type | Action list | loop |
|---|---|---|---|
| `e`   | PAGE_START | `a` Logo Animation | **true** |
| `e-3` | PAGE_START | `a-3` Hero Animations | false |
| `e-5` | MOUSE_CLICK on replay btn | `a-4` Play Chart | false |

- `a` (marquee): 3 groups, x 0% -> -50% (25000ms) -> 0% (0ms),
  `useFirstGroupAsInitialState:true`. Equivalent to ONE infinite linear 25s
  0%->-50% `element.animate()`. Markup already contains 2 copies of the strip,
  which is why -50% wraps seamlessly — **never clone a third set**.
- `a-3` (hero): opacity fades on `...b376` (hero__cta), `...b395`, and
  `355463fa-...-5720`. **That third target does not exist in the static markup**
  (A/B'd out) — must no-op gracefully but still honour its group timing.
- `a-4` (chart replay): G1 hide replay btn (display none + opacity 0) at
  delay 0; G2 `PLUGIN_RIVE` trigger `onRestart` at delay 100; G3 reveal btn
  (display flex, opacity 1, 300ms) at delay 10000.

IX2 semantics: items within a group run concurrently honouring own delays;
groups run sequentially, next starts after current group's longest
(delay+duration). First group is instant initial state when
`useFirstGroupAsInitialState`.

## Site-specific modules written (9 total, all in app/lib/)
`coframeCursor` (script-24 retype engine), `coframeSwipers` (case-studies +
introduction tabs), `coframeNav` (scroll darkening + mobile menu + dropdown),
`coframeForms` (hero waitlist), `coframeNewsletter` (script-20), `coframeFadeIn`
(script-21), `coframeMarquee` (IX2 `a`), `coframeHeroAnim` (IX2 `a-3`),
`coframeRive` (chart + IX2 `a-4`).

## Generic template effects DROPPED and why (do not re-add)
- `initNavToggle` / `initNavScroll` / `initNavDropdown` — `coframeNav.ts:18`
  owns `.w-nav-menu`, and initNavToggle's default selector is
  `.w-nav-button, ... ` + `.w-nav-menu` -> **double owner** on the same elements.
  Also no `.w-dropdown` exists here at all (dropdown is hand-built).
- `initTabs` — would double-bind the same `.introduction__step` elements
  `coframeSwipers` owns.
- `initMarquee` — its `[class*="marquee"]` selector matches FIVE nested classes
  here (`.logo-marquee`, `__animation-container`, `__logos`, `__logo`,
  `__logo-item`) and would clone children at several levels at once.
- `createFadeIn` — wrong selector/threshold/stagger (see below).
KEPT: `smoothAnchors`, `accordion`, `counters`, `lazyImages` (no-ops or safe),
plus `createForms({ formSelector: '.newsletter-form__form' })` scoped to the
newsletter form ONLY, as the interception layer.

## Real bug caught at the verification gate (would have shipped broken)
`.newsletter-form__button` is an **`<a href="#">`, not a submit control**
(`hasSubmitButton: false`, `method="post"`, no action). The generic
`createForms` binds `submit`, which that anchor never fires — so the newsletter
button did nothing AND the bare `#` jumped the page to top. `initSmoothAnchors`
does NOT cover it: its selector is `a[href^="#"]:not([href="#"])`, deliberately
excluding bare `#`. Fix: ported `script-20.js` into `coframeNewsletter.ts`
(click -> preventDefault -> validate -> `form.requestSubmit()`, plus Enter-key
path, plus upstream's `alert()`), registered BEFORE the generic interceptor.
`requestSubmit()` (not `submit()`) is essential — it fires a cancelable submit
event the interceptor can catch.
Verified live after fix: no navigation, `hash: ""`, scrollY stayed 11761,
`.w-form-done` -> "You're in! Time to fuel your growth 🚀", fail block none.

## Faithful-quirk decisions (deliberate, don't "fix")
- `coframeFadeIn`: upstream `script-21.js` uses selector `.fade-in` ONLY,
  threshold **0.4** (not template default 0.15), and a `data-fade-delay`
  keyword map s/m/l/xl = 0.4/0.8/1.2/1.6s -> `style.animationDelay`.
  Active class is `.faded-in`.
- Upstream reassigns ONE shared `observer` var inside the per-element loop, so
  each callback closes over the last observer and `unobserve` mostly no-ops.
  Reproduced verbatim rather than fixed.
- `hero__cta` (`...b376`) is BOTH an IX2 `a-3` target AND a `.fade-in` element
  with `data-fade-delay="l"`. Upstream really does run both; overlap preserved.
- `.newsletter-form__form` has `display: flex !important` in upstream CSS, so
  the interceptor's inline `display:none` is overridden and form+done block
  both show. Upstream behaves identically — not a bug.

## Known-good false positives (don't chase these next run)
- **`animations 47/48`** in viewport-check: harness counts
  `.fade-in, [data-fade], [data-aos], [data-animate], [data-scroll]` = 48, but
  exactly 1 element (`<div data-fade="" className="compare-grid">` in
  CompareSection.tsx) has a bare `data-fade` and no `.fade-in`. Proven by count:
  47 `.fade-in` + 1 bare `data-fade`. Faithful port correctly excludes it.
- **ipad-pro overflow is an UPSTREAM bug we correctly do NOT inherit**: live
  1051 vs 1024 (+27px), caused by `div.cursor-container` (w=1051, right=1051).
  Local is 1024/1024 with no cursor-container in `tooWide` (emptySelectors +
  template cursor width/height fix). Live ipad-mini reporting innerWidth 928 at
  a 768 viewport is the same root cause.
- "55 unmapped fonts" pipeline warning: false positive (45 fonts on disk,
  3/3 spot-checked present).
- `script-13.js` is JSON-LD, not Rive ("drives" grep false positive).
- `.swiper-variants` appears in the source script but NOT in generated markup —
  only 2 real swiper roots exist (case-studies + introduction).

## Rive: three constraints, each independently fatal
1. Must be `@rive-app/webgl2@2.35.0`. Under `@rive-app/canvas` the canvas is
   silently blank — no exception, no console error.
2. Config attrs live on a **wrapper div** `div.impact__animation[data-rive-url]`
   with a bare `<canvas>` child. A `canvas[data-rive-url]` selector (the generic
   adapter's default) matches nothing and the chart never mounts.
3. Animation is **trigger-driven**: state machine idles until trigger input
   `onRestart` fires. Never call reset()/play() before `onLoad` — on a
   not-yet-loaded instance it never returns (queued task re-adds itself to the
   queue it's draining) and wedges the main thread.
Also: `.impact__replay-button` starts CSS-visible (`display:flex`, sanitizer
stripped the captured inline `opacity:0;display:none`), so IX2 `a-4` group 1
must be applied at init or the button sits on top of the chart on first paint.
`script-29.js` fires the first play via `replayButton.click()` on
DOMContentLoaded — already fired before React mounts, so trigger it from Rive's
own `onLoad` instead. wasm self-hosted at `/assets/rive/rive-webgl2.wasm`
(verified byte-identical via `cmp` to node_modules copy); removed an orphaned
duplicate `rive.96db8912.wasm` referenced only by asset-map.json.

## Corrected stale note from a prior run
`.introduction.swiper .swiper-wrapper` hover-pause selector is **LIVE**, not
dead — static markup carries `swiper-wrapper` on `introduction__steps`.

args.content:
# Website-replica: Webflow IX2 recovery + the anchor-as-submit trap

Generalizable lessons from repeated coframe.com replica runs. Applies to ANY
Webflow-built target, and the form trap applies to any target.

## 1. Recover Webflow IX2 interactions from the minified chunk
The sanitizer strips `webflow.js`, which means **every IX2 interaction silently
disappears** (marquees, entrance fades, click choreography). There are often no
`@keyframes` for these at all, so nothing in the CSS hints they existed. If a
replica looks static compared to live, suspect IX2 before suspecting CSS.

Extract the real payload with node from `scrape/raw/js/webflow.schunk.*.js`:
- locate `actionLists:{a:{id:"a"`
- then `lastIndexOf("events:{")` before that offset — the `events` object is
  small (~1-2KB) and can be printed raw and read directly.

You need BOTH objects: `actionLists` gives the animation steps, `events` gives
the trigger (`PAGE_START` / `MOUSE_CLICK` / etc.) **and the `loop` flag**, which
lives on the event's `config`, not on the action list. Don't infer the trigger.

IX2 execution semantics to reproduce:
- Items **within** a group run concurrently, each honouring its own `delay`.
- Groups run **sequentially**; the next starts after the current group's longest
  `(delay + duration)`.
- `useFirstGroupAsInitialState: true` -> group 1 is applied **instantly** as an
  initial state, not animated.
- A whole 3-group loop of `x: 0% -> -50% (long) -> 0% (0ms)` collapses to ONE
  infinite linear `element.animate()`. Simplify rather than emulate the runtime.

Targets are matched by `data-w-id`. **Expect some targets not to exist** in the
captured markup (A/B testing, personalization). Skip missing elements but still
honour their group timing, so downstream groups stay in phase.

## 2. The anchor-as-submit-button trap (bit me for real)
Webflow forms frequently use `<a href="#">` as the submit control with an inline
script doing `preventDefault()` + validate + `form.requestSubmit()`. A generic
form effect that binds the `submit` event **will never fire**, so the form does
nothing AND the bare `#` jumps the page to the top.

Always check before trusting a generic form effect:
```js
form.querySelector('button[type="submit"], input[type="submit"]')  // false => trap
```
Note also that a typical `initSmoothAnchors` uses
`a[href^="#"]:not([href="#"])`, which **deliberately excludes bare `#`** — so it
will not save you here either.

Fix pattern: port the upstream click handler, and keep two clean layers —
the port owns validation + **triggering**, the generic form effect owns
**intercepting** (so nothing is POSTed to someone else's CRM). Use
`form.requestSubmit()`, never `form.submit()`: only the former fires a
cancelable `submit` event the interception layer can catch.

## 3. Double-owner check before registering generic effects
Before registering any generic effect, compare its DEFAULT SELECTOR against what
the site-specific port already binds. Real collisions hit:
- generic navToggle default (`.w-nav-button` + `.w-nav-menu`) vs a hand-ported
  nav module that already owns `.w-nav-menu`.
- generic tabs vs a ported swiper/tab engine on the same step elements.
- generic marquee `[class*="marquee"]` matching FIVE nested classes on one
  component, cloning children at several levels at once.
Grep the port for its `querySelector` calls and diff against the generic
defaults. Two owners on one element is a real, hard-to-debug bug.

## 4. Distinguish upstream bugs from your own regressions
Run the live-vs-local viewport comparison and read the per-element overflow
list, not just the pass/fail. An overflow present on LIVE but absent locally is
usually an upstream bug your config correctly suppresses (e.g. a
cursor-tracking overlay neutralized via `emptySelectors`) — that's a pass, not a
gap. Conversely, verify your own numbers: a harness "N-1/N animations" warning
is often the harness's broader selector counting an element the faithful port
intentionally excludes. Prove it by counting both selectors in the markup.

## 5. Verification-gate habits that paid off
- Page HEIGHT equality between local and live at every viewport is a much
  stronger layout signal than the pixel-diff percentage.
- Always eyeball the composites. A ~1% diff was entirely animation phase and
  A/B copy; in one shot local rendered the chart while LIVE was still at `$0`,
  which positively proved the canvas/Rive port worked.
- Distrust subagent prose; re-verify claims against files and tool output.
- After changing app code, the running prod server still serves the OLD build —
  rebuild and restart before re-testing in the browser.
- Check computed style vs inline style before declaring a bug: upstream
  `display: flex !important` can override an interceptor's inline `display:none`
  and that's faithful, not broken.

blocks.text:
# Done — `coframecom-3` is complete and verified 🐾

All 8 checklist items green, server torn down, nothing left listening on 3302. Tail wagging hard on this one — the verification gate actually caught a real bug before it shipped.

## What was built

A pixel-faithful Next.js + TypeScript replica of `https://www.coframe.com/` in `coframecom-3/`, running on port 3302, making **zero remote requests at runtime**.

- **Pipeline**: 16 sections, 31 stylesheets, 160 assets self-hosted (45 fonts, 90 images, 2 Rive files).
- **`captureMode: "static"`** chosen deliberately (ratio 0.82, 1176/1439 elements) to avoid baking in the runtime-generated duplicate nodes that broke an earlier run, with `emptySelectors`/`unwrapSelectors` as a defensive belt.
- **9 site-specific effect modules** written in `app/lib/`, each documenting the exact upstream source it was transcribed from.

## Headline results

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run verify` | exit 0 — tsc clean, **34/34** tests, 4/4 static pages |
| `npm run viewports` | **7/7 PASS**, canvas `painted=true` everywhere, 2 carousels, 119 images 0 broken |
| `npm run compare` | avg **0.82%** diff; **local page height == live exactly at all 7 viewports** |
| Autoscroll regression | `scrollY` held at **exactly 5200** across 16s while the swiper advanced to index 3 |

## The most valuable find: recovering Webflow IX2

`webflow.js` is stripped by the sanitizer, so *all* IX2 motion vanishes silently — and there are no `@keyframes` to hint it ever existed. I extracted the real payload out of the minified `webflow.schunk.*.js` and reconstructed the full trigger map:

| Event | Type | Action list | loop |
|---|---|---|---|
| `e` | PAGE_START | `a` Logo Animation | **true** |
| `e-3` | PAGE_START | `a-3` Hero Animations | false |
| `e-5` | MOUSE_CLICK | `a-4` Play Chart | false |

This produced the marquee, hero entrance fades, and the Rive replay choreography. One `a-3` target doesn't exist in the markup (A/B'd out) — it no-ops gracefully while still honouring its group timing so later groups stay in phase.

## A real bug caught at the gate

`.newsletter-form__button` is an **`<a href="#">`, not a submit control**. The generic form effect binds `submit`, which that anchor never fires — so the newsletter did nothing *and* the bare `#` jumped the page to top. `initSmoothAnchors` doesn't cover it either (its selector deliberately excludes bare `#`). I ported `script-20.js` into `coframeNewsletter.ts` and split ownership cleanly: the port validates and **triggers** via `requestSubmit()`, the generic effect **intercepts** so nothing is ever POSTed. Verified live afterwards: no navigation, empty hash, scroll held at 11761, done block revealed.

## Two things I want to flag as *not* bugs

- **`47/48` animations** — the harness counts a broader selector; exactly one element (`<div data-fade className="compare-grid">`) has a bare `data-fade` and no `.fade-in`. My faithful port correctly excludes it, proven by counting both.
- **ipad-pro overflow is an upstream bug I correctly don't inherit** — live overflows +27px via `div.cursor-container`; local is a clean 1024/1024.

I also fixed a genuine template bug (`manifest.source` was hardcoded and lied whenever `captureMode` was static) in **both** this run and the vendored template, so future runs inherit it. Notes written to project and global memory, including the IX2 extraction recipe and the anchor-as-submit trap.

One caveat worth stating plainly: the `compare` composites were generated against the pre-newsletter build. I re-ran the **viewport** gate against the final build (7/7 PASS) and `verify` after the change, but did not regenerate the pixel composites — the newsletter fix only adds footer event listeners, so I'd expect no visual delta, though I haven't proven that with a fresh diff.
